text:
The Philadelphia Eagles will be without their starting quarterback this Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, as the team has ruled out Jalen Hurts due to a superficial blood clot.

On Thursday, the Eagles announced that it was believed that Hurts suffered a calf injury during the Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. After the team traveled to London for their Week 5 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars, Hurts underwent an ultrasound that revealed a blood clot. The Eagles' medical staff and doctors concluded Hurts was safe to suit up and play, but did inform the league office about the situation.

During a follow-up ultrasound on Wednesday of this week, the staff discovered movement in Hurts' blood clot, which led the team to rule him out for Sunday.

Read the Eagles' full statement below:

"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter.

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

This is something that will have to be monitored closely, and it could force Hurts to miss more than one game. Just hours before the Eagles discovered movement in the blood clot, Hurts addressed the "calf injury" that led him to be listed on the injury report last Friday and on Wednesday.

"It was a very unique experience, to say the least," Hurts said. "I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game."

The Eagles did not go into detail about the clot, but this could be classified as "superficial thrombophlebitis," per Harvard Health Publishing. This is different than "deep vein thrombosis," which is a much more serious condition that requires anti-clotting drugs. We've seen several cases of deep vein thrombosis in the NBA, including with Spurs superstar Victor Wembanyama, who missed the final 30 games of the 2024-25 season after doctors discovered deep vein thrombosis in his right shoulder. As for superficial thrombophlebitis, Harvard Health Publishing says it can improve over the course of one week to several weeks. Each case is different.

With Hurts out, Tanner McKee is expected to start under center for the Eagles. He's 1-1 in his two career starts over the last two years and has played in a total of six NFL games. In the 2024 regular-season finale, the former sixth-round pick out of Stanford impressed in a 20-13 win over the Giants. McKee completed 27 of 41 passes for 269 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions.

Philly also has rookie Cole Payton on the roster. He was selected in the fifth round of this year's draft out of North Dakota State.

While the Eagles just released Andy Dalton last week, NFL Media reports that the veteran is an option to return. He's reportedly been in contact with a few teams, but he's familiar with Nick Sirianni's offense if the Eagles decide to go that route.

Through five games, Hurts has completed 57.8% of his passes for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in a 2-3 start. Sunday's loss to the Jaguars in London snapped a franchise-record streak of 76 games where the Eagles were .500 or better, per CBS Sports Research.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, the team announced Thursday.

Hurts was listed as a full participant in Friday's practice before the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with a calf injury. He had no injury designation for Sunday's game in London.

The Eagles released a statement detailing the process that led to the discovery of the blood clot.

"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf," the team said. "He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report.

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia."

The Eagles said Hurts "played without limitation" against the Jaguars before receiving treatment Monday and Tuesday then practicing in full Wednesday.

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority," the Eagles said.

The Eagles have remained in communication with the NFL office throughout the process, the team said.

Asked about the injury Wednesday, Hurts indicated he got "nicked" against the Rams while hinting that the lead-up to the Jaguars game was not ordinary.

"It was a very unique experience, to say the least. I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game," he said.

Hurts did not take the field until right before the opening kickoff against Jacksonville and rode the stationary bike between series. He indicated both actions were related to the calf. He completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.

Tanner McKee is expected to start in place of Hurts against the Panthers.

The 28-year-old Hurts has 933 passing yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season. He has led the Eagles to two Super Bowl appearances and earned MVP honors after they beat the Kansas City Chiefs to win the championship in the 2024 season.

Hurts is in the midst of a five-year, $255 million extension, including $179.3 million guaranteed, with the Eagles that takes him through the 2028 season.

The Eagles stunned fans when they drafted Hurts out of Oklahoma in the second round in 2020. They seemingly had Carson Wentz entrenched at QB and had more pressing needs. Hurt was expected to serve as insurance for Wentz. Instead, he supplanted him and became one of the top young quarterbacks in the NFL.

text:
Thursday’s “First Call” checks on Baker Mayfield’s health in advance of the Pittsburgh Steelers’ game in Tampa on Sunday. Some Pitt, Penn State and Duquesne alumni are also on the Buccaneers’ injured list.

The NFL addresses concerns about the Steelers-Saints game in Paris next week. Aaron Rodgers addresses concerns about the Steelers’ wide receiver room this week.

We also get an update on Lamar Jackson’s recovery ahead of the Cleveland-Baltimore showdown in the AFC North.

Working back

Both the Steelers (3-2) and Buccaneers (1-4) had lengthy injury reports to start the week. Several players on both teams didn’t practice at all, with two more workdays to go.

On the Steelers’ side, Keeanu Benton, Jalen Ramsey, Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson all missed practice entirely with various injuries. Cameron Heyward had a rest day. Skowronek and Wilson are expected to miss the game, based on Mike McCarthy’s statements Monday.

As for Tampa Bay, plenty of familiar names didn’t practice. They include quarterback Baker Mayfield, cornerback Ayden Garnes (Duquesne/WVU), running back Sean Tucker and defensive back Antoine Winfield Jr. Former Penn State receiver Chris Godwin also sat out for a rest day. Ex-Pitt linebacker SirVocea Dennis was limited with ankle and foot injuries.

Mayfield was supposed to be out for three to six weeks with his thumb injury. Last week, he was reportedly hoping to push it to come back for the Pittsburgh game. If he can’t go, Jalon Daniels will start at quarterback.

“Nothing has changed,” coach Todd Bowles said following practice. “He’s getting better. We’ll see how much he throws and how he looks.”

According to the Tampa Bay Times, Bowles said of Mayfield: “If he’s not 100%, he doesn’t need to play.”

No help on the way

Based on how Aaron Rodgers spoke Wednesday, don’t expect the Steelers to add any wide receiver help anytime soon.

That’s despite injuries to Skowronek, Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr.

“It seems like at this point it’s just in-house options. We’ve got a talented (practice) squad group of guys and guys who played football at the highest level and made plays. Excited about getting those guys in,” Rodgers said. “(Brandon) Smith, Brandon Johnson, maybe Isaiah (Hodgins). We’ll get some guys who haven’t seen a lot of time out there and expect them to play well.”

The quarterback also suggested that the tight ends could increase their roles, including Robert Tonyan, who has been used sparingly since being acquired this offseason. He has one catch for 2 yards on one target this season.

“Obviously, (Tonyan) has played a lot of football and played at a high level, so I’m sure he’ll get some more opportunities,” Rodgers added.

Pat Freiermuth had two touchdowns last week. He and Darnell Washington combined for seven catches and 56 yards against the Colts.

More sports

• Steelers excelling in yards after catch because of tackle-breaking, accurate passing

• Pitt tight end Carson Kent embracing expanded role in offense

• Mark Madden: Mike McCarthy can be trusted to make right decisions for Steelers

Familiar foe

Elsewhere in the AFC North, the Cincinnati Bengals are idle this weekend, and the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns play each other.

That means the Ravens will be facing former offensive coordinator Todd Monken. He’s now coaching the Browns.

When asked if Monken is preparing for Lamar Jackson at quarterback, Monken said, “I think you prepare for the Ravens.”

Jackson is dealing with an ankle injury and missed last week’s win in Atlanta. Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic quoted Baltimore coach Jesse Minter as saying that Jackson is day-to-day and “when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice.”

Still on

The Steelers’ game against New Orleans next week is still scheduled to take place in Paris. That’s despite a wave of protests in France.

The league issued a statement to ESPN’s Brooke Pryor that it is still “excited” to have the game overseas.

According to The New York Times, the protests are by students acting out “against poor school conditions and teacher shortages.”

If it is determined that the contest can’t be played in Paris, New Orleans is the designated home team, so the game may well shift to the Caesars Superdome.

TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice Wednesday to rest his ailing left ankle and his status for Sunday's game against the Rams isn't clear as of yet, coach Mike LaFleur said.

The plan, LaFleur said, is to take Love's ankle "one day at a time," but the Cardinals understand for it to fully heal, the third-overall pick needs to stay off it.

"We all are in agreeance as much as he wants to battle through, we're all in agreeance right now, it's just, hey just give it a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that'll entail for Sunday."

Love's style of play, however, makes it difficult for him to prevent the injury from lingering, LaFleur intimated.

"I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this, too," LaFleur said, "but he's a tough dude. "

But you guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. And, I mean, imagine being a back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you're capable of?"

Asked whether he was concerned about Love's injury lingering, LaFleur swiftly pointed out which body part was injured.

"They're ankles. It's an ankle," LaFleur said. "So, you don't know. I'm not a doctor and each body's a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. I mean, he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it's just lingered."

Love has rushed for 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 carries this season for an average of 3.7 yards per carry. He's also contributed 36 receiving yards and a touchdown on 11 catches. His best game to date came in Week 3 at San Francisco, when he ran for 89 yards.

The Notre Dame star rushed for just 22 yards in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions on 12 carries.

LaFleur said, in some ways, Love's explosiveness has been affected by the ankle injury in recent weeks.

"You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur said. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So, I mean, I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again, the rest for him is going to be vital."

text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- When Adonai Mitchell injured a finger in practice before Week 3, the New York Jets decided not to put the wide receiver on injured reserve, thinking he'd be back within four weeks.

As it turned out, Mitchell underwent surgery about a week later, coach Aaron Glenn revealed Wednesday, and now is expected to miss his fourth consecutive game.

Mitchell is still considered week-to-week, according to Glenn. It means Tim Patrick, who returned last week from a four-week stint on IR, likely will start alongside Garrett Wilson when the Jets (2-3) face the New England Patriots (3-2) on Sunday at Gillette Stadium.

Rookie Omar Cooper Jr., who has missed four games with a high ankle sprain, also could be a factor as he was designated to return from IR.

Mitchell's injury has been a mystery. Glenn has been evasive, claiming last week that he didn't know if the finger was fractured or sprained and saying there was no surgery. On Wednesday, Glenn opened his news conference by saying he wanted to provide "some clarity" on the injury.

"So he did have a small procedure on his hand," Glenn said. "But the good thing is, man, he's moving his fingers around really, really well."

Glenn said Mitchell waited about a week to 10 days before opting for surgery because he wanted "to see how he progressed and then wanted to go ahead and get it knocked out."

Mitchell has remained on the 53-man roster. The Jets could've put him on IR when the injury occurred, which would've created a roster spot for another player. He had nine receptions for 122 yards in the first two games. Since then, the Jets' receivers not named Wilson have produced only seven receptions and one touchdown.

The Jets are hopeful that Cooper, one of the team's three first-round draft picks this spring, can contribute immediately. He lasted only five snaps in the opener before injuring his ankle. One of those plays was a dazzling catch-and-run that covered 30 yards.

"Obviously, he's a really good player, but you never want any rookie to actually miss time because the reps are valuable for these guys," Glenn said of Cooper.

title: Update on NFL Concussion Litigation - Jinks Crow
description:
On August 28, 2011, Derek Sheely died as a result of second-impact syndrome.
This syndrome occurs when the brain swells rapidly after a person suffers a second concussion before symptoms from an earlier concussion have subsided.
The settlement provides that the Defendants will pay $1,200,000.00 to The Derek Sheely Foundation.
The NCAA and FSU, in conjunction with The Derek Sheely Foundation, agreed to sponsor and fund a symposium in honor of Derek Sheely.

text:
Now that football season is here, we should be mindful that the highest priority of the game should be the safety and well-being of the athletes. Unfortunately, this has not always been the case.

On August 28, 2011, Derek Sheely died as a result of second-impact syndrome. This syndrome occurs when the brain swells rapidly after a person suffers a second concussion before symptoms from an earlier concussion have subsided. On August 22, 2013, the family of Derek Sheely filed a wrongful death lawsuit against the NCAA, Kranos, George L. Heider, Inc., two Frostburg State University coaches, and a Frostburg State athletic trainer, asserting that Derek’s death was a preventable tragedy.

Last month, the Parties announced that a settlement was reached. The settlement provides that the Defendants will pay $1,200,000.00 to The Derek Sheely Foundation. In addition to this payment, the Parties agreed to the following terms that are aimed at increasing awareness and research about concussions.

The NCAA and FSU, in conjunction with The Derek Sheely Foundation, agreed to sponsor and fund a symposium in honor of Derek Sheely. It will focus on the reduction of catastrophic risk to student-athletes and will be presented to coaches, trainers, sports medicine personnel, student-athletes, youth, and parents.

FSU will establish an annual Derek Sheely Foundation fundraiser on campus.

FSU will provide sufficient funding to enable The Derek Thomson Sheely Leadership Award to be increased to a full-tuition scholarship for a minimum of 10 years, and potentially longer, to begin on or before the 2017-2018 academic year.

The NCAA and FSU, in conjunction with The Derek Sheely Foundation, will make a research award for a project dealing with catastrophic risk.

FSU will retire Derek Sheely’s number and display it in a location on campus.

The NCAA will continue to discuss with its member institutions policies regarding concussion guideline enforcement, concussion, and second-impact syndrome training for coaches and trainers, and elimination of certain drills.

The NCAA will produce a new video addressing risks of head injuries, including second-impact syndrome, in sports that will be available to member institutions on or before June 1, 2017.

Paul Anderson, the attorney for the Sheely Foundation, stated: “This is a tremendous result that will guarantee that The Derek Sheely Foundation will be able to continue its mission of protecting the health and safety of athletes, while also ensuring that Derek’s legacy lives on through the Foundation. This unprecedented litigation and subsequent settlement have solidified that second-impact syndrome is not an inherent risk of sport and that those who are responsible for the safety of athletes must take affirmative action to prevent a tragedy like Derek’s from ever happening again.”

Hopefully, this senseless tragedy will not be in vain. Because of the work of the Sheely Foundation and others to educate and train coaches and their staff, the risks associated with football and other sports can be minimized. This landmark settlement will no doubt go a long way in that regard.

title: Jalen Hurts won't say much about "very unique" calf injury that was disclosed last Friday
description:
Quarterback Jalen Hurts was listed as fully participating in Friday’s practice before the game against the Jaguars with a calf injury.
He had no injury designation for Sunday’s game in London, and he was never downgraded to questionable or doubtful.
What would be “very unique” about a calf injury that didn’t impact his practice reps?
Hurts was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice, due to the calf injury.
And the NFL doesn’t require much more than the bare-bones contents of the injury report.
text:
Last week’s injury report for the Eagles included a curious designation on Friday. And Wednesday’s comments from the player at the center of the issue served only to make it more curious.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts was listed as fully participating in Friday’s practice before the game against the Jaguars with a calf injury. He had no injury designation for Sunday’s game in London, and he was never downgraded to questionable or doubtful.

When the question came up during his midweek press conference, here’s what Hurts said: “It was a very unique experience, to say the least. I don’t want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game.”

There’s a lot there, in not that many words. What would be “very unique” about a calf injury that didn’t impact his practice reps? And why would it be a big secret?

The complicating factor is that the Eagles flew to London on Friday. Did he require medical care in London? Would it be something that the team doctors were able to provide? Did he have to visit a local hospital for it?

He said he was “nicked up” during the Rams game, but he wasn’t on the injury report for Wednesday or Thursday. Was is it that could have happened on Sunday that would have resulted in symptoms on Friday. (A condition like compartment syndrome typically surfaces much more quickly.)

Regardless, plenty of questions flow from what seems to be very innocuous and basic on the surface. Hurts’s words deepen the mystery.

He remains on the Week 6 injury report, in advance of Sunday’s game against the Panthers. Hurts was listed as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice, due to the calf injury.

Whatever the explanation is, there’s clearly more to the story than what the team has disclosed. And the NFL doesn’t require much more than the bare-bones contents of the injury report.

description:

Jackson was absent again from the portion of Ravens practice open to reporters, but there's a "realistic chance" he plays Sunday against the Cleveland Browns.
Running back Saquon Barkley and Wide Receiver DeVonta Smith both sat out again Wednesday as the Eagles opened their practice week ahead of Sunday’s game against the Panthers, both still nursing hamstring injuries.
Before his injury, Penix was having a strong outing, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown.
With both Atlanta and Chicago sitting at 3-2, Caleb Williams and Penix are set to face off in a must-win game for both sides.
text:
Wednesday in the NFL brought updates on two quarterbacks working their way back from injury.

The Baltimore Ravens and Chicago Bears provided updates on their situations ahead of the weekend. Lamar Jackson is inching closer to a return for the Ravens, while Caleb Williams took a real step forward in Chicago.

Jackson was absent again from the portion of Ravens practice open to reporters, but there's a "realistic chance" he plays Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, Williams was a full participant in the Bears’ Wednesday walkthrough, the clearest sign yet that he could be back under center against the Atlanta Falcons.

Here’s the latest from around the NFL on Wednesday.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams took a real step toward returning for Sunday’s game against the Falcons, serving as a full participant in Chicago’s Wednesday walkthrough after missing the past three weeks with a hamstring injury.

It’s a positive sign that Williams could be back on the field soon, but head coach Ben Johnson didn't rush to say his return would come against Atlanta when asked who would start under center this week.

"It’s still fluid," Johnson told reporters, "but I feel good about the plan that we have in place at this point."

Williams showed progress last week, logging a limited practice and working through pregame warm-ups as he inches closer to a return.

The 2022 Heisman Trophy winner was initially expected to miss three to four games after injuring his hamstring in Week 2, and the Bears went 2-1 without him, with backups Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent each starting and picking up a win, though Bagent struggled in last week’s 31-7 loss to the Packers.

Johnson also acknowledged the tight turnaround before Chicago’s Thursday night game against the Falcons could factor into how the team handles the quarterback's workload regardless of who starts.

"I don't know that any of them are exactly 100% at this point of the season, so that's something that we certainly look at," Johnson said.

Running back Saquon Barkley and Wide Receiver DeVonta Smith both sat out again Wednesday as the Eagles opened their practice week ahead of Sunday’s game against the Panthers, both still nursing hamstring injuries.

Barkley missed last week’s game in London after playing just four snaps against the Rams the week prior, and Smith has now missed the last two games.

Philadelphia’s offense has cratered without its two biggest weapons as the Eagles have managed just 404 total yards over those two losses.

Earlier in the week, head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters he was "hopeful" one or both could return this week.

The need is especially urgent at running back, where backup Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve and third-stringer Will Shipley is now expected to miss multiple weeks with a foot injury suffered against the Jaguars.

That left Philadelphia finishing that game with two practice-squad call-ups, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele, and just 22 rushing yards on 18 carries — the team’s lowest rushing output in a game since 2015.

Barkley and Smith are far from the only Eagles players dealing with injuries as six players sat out Wednesday’s practice in total, while 11 other players were limited participants. Seven more Eagles players were listed as full participants on Wednesday's injury report, including quarterback Jalen Hurts (calf).

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was missing again from the open portion of Ravens' practice Wednesday as he continues working back from the ankle injury that’s already cost him one game.

Ravens Head Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday that Jackson was "definitely day-to-day" adding, "To Lamar’s credit, he’s working his butt off and he's doing everything he can to be out here." ESPN reported Wednesday that Jackson has a "realistic chance" to play Sunday.

Jackson went down two weeks ago in a win over the Titans, sacked on the final play of the first half with a sprained left ankle. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before having to leave the game.

Tyler Huntley has stepped in his place after filling in for Jackson nearly half of last season, throwing for 201 yards and two scores and rushing for the winning touchdown in overtime of last week’s win over the Falcons.

At 4-1, Baltimore has some margin to be careful with Jackson’s return, especially after last season’s hamstring injury lingered well past his initial comeback.

Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. isn't expected to be sidelined long after exiting late against the Baltimore Ravens with a rib injury.

Since suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 1, wide receiver A.J. Brown has been on injured reserve, but his return could take place as early as Sunday. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced Wednesday that Brown has been designated to return to practice.

Brown returned to practice on Wednesday in a limited capacity as he works his way back to full strength.

The Patriots acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason for a 2028 first-round pick. The offense has had plenty of ups and downs since his injury, but both Romeo Doubs and Efton Chism III have seen steady improvements in production since.

Getting Brown back into an improving offense will be huge for Drake Maye as the Patriots push to stay competitive in the AFC playoff picture.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters on Wednesday that Michael Penix Jr. is expected to start against the Chicago Bears, barring any setbacks. Since entering the league, he has struggled to stay healthy, so avoiding missed time is a positive sign for both Penix and the Falcons.

Following Penix’s exit against the Ravens, backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa came in and threw a game-ending interception in overtime. Before his injury, Penix was having a strong outing, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown.

Through his first three starts this season, Penix is off to the best stretch of his career, especially impressive considering he's returning from a season-ending knee injury. He's completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and just one interception.

Keeping Penix on the field is massive for a Falcons team competing in a wide-open NFC South. With both Atlanta and Chicago sitting at 3-2, Caleb Williams and Penix are set to face off in a must-win game for both sides.

text:
Baylor maintains its NFL presence in 2026. Two defensive stars from the 2021 Big 12 Championship team continue to shine in the NFL, while Josh Cameron, a former walk-on from Cedar Park, continues his story by stepping up as a Swiss Army knife for the Jaguars. Tyquan Thornton had his surgery this past week, and we will all be hoping for a speedy recovery for the Kansas City Chiefs receiver.

Josh Cameron (WR) - Jacksonville Jaguars

Josh Cameron received six targets from quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the game in London against the Eagles. He hauled in three of those passes, totaling 43 yards. Josh Cameron's highlight play, a kick return at the start of the game, was called back due to a penalty. Josh had another key special teams play where he laid down a key block on the final kick return of the game, which put the Jaguars in field goal range and won the game.

Josh Cameron's targets seem to increase every week, and with Brian Thomas Jr. struggling to step into his role as WR2, many Jaguars fans are calling for Cameron to step up into that role.

Jalen Pitre (S) - Houston Texans

Jalen Pitre had three tackles in the Texans' first win of the season this past Sunday. Unfortunately, Pitre left the game injured in the second half. Fortunately for the Texans and for Pitre, the injury will not require surgery, and he will be assessed on a week-to-week basis. The Texans need to gain some momentum here, and Pitre is undoubtedly a leader in this Texans defense and will need to step up to change the tide of the season in Houston.

Terrel Bernard (LB) - Buffalo Bills

Terrel Bernard had a good game for the Bills against the best offense in the league. He had seven total tackles and a good hit on Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford. Bernard and the Bills pulled off a win, but the Bills defense still has some work to do if the Bills want to make a deep playoff run.

James Lynch (DL) - Chicago Bears

text:
The Eagles opened the practice window Wednesday for three-time Pro Bowl left guard Landon Dickerson, who hasn’t played since a disastrous opening-day performance against Washington.

Dickerson was placed on Injured Reserve with a bone bruise in his right knee a day after the season opener, in which he admitted he was a “complete liability” because the injury hampered him so much. He said he suffered the injury during training camp and thought it would heal on its own.

“You guys know Landon well, he works hard, he's determined to get back, and I think he's done a nice job taking care of his body to get himself back,” Sirianni said Wednesday before the news was made official. “Landon's a hell of a player and he's been a hell of a player for us.”

Once placed on Injured Reserve, players must miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. With his practice window, Dickerson is able to practice with the team while remaining on IR until he’s officially activated.

With Dickerson unavailable, the Eagles’ initially moved Cam Jurgens from center to left guard and inserted 2nd-year pro Drew Kendall at center. They ultimately traded Jurgens to the Ravens, and with Kendall out Sunday with a knee injury, they wound up with two undrafted players making their first career start on the o-line, Willie Lampkin at left guard and Jake Majors at center.

Left tackle Jordan Mailata and right guard Tyler Steen have started all five games, but the Eagles have used three left guards (Dickerson, Jurgens, Lampkin), three centers (Jurgens, Kendall, Majors) and two right tackles (Lane Johnson, Markel Bell). So they’ve had nine different o-line starters and four different offensive lines through Week 5.

The Packers are the only team that’s used more starting offensive linemen. They’ve had 10 different starters this year. The Chargers have also used nine starters, including former Eagle Kayode Awosika.

Philadelphia Eagles

Find the latest Philadelphia Eagles news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Philadelphia.

If Dickerson is able to play Sunday against the Panthers, he would presumably move back into his left guard spot in place of Lampkin. The center could be either Kendall if he’s healthy, Lampkin or Majors.

Dickerson, the Eagles’ 2nd-round pick in 2021, is one of 10 players in franchise history and the only offensive lineman to make three Pro Bowls in his first four seasons, the first since Donovan McNabb from 2000 through 2002.

Although he’s battled injuries his entire college and pro career, Dickerson had only missed four games because of injuries in his first five seasons before going on IR Sept. 15.

But last year was a difficult year for Dickerson, who played hurt all year and missed the Pro Bowl for the first time since his rookie year.

“The best plan moving forward is to put me on I.R. so I can get this thing better to have a good stretch at the back end of the season vs. kind of what happened last year and limp it through for 18 weeks,” Dickerson said on WIP when he went on IR. “I don't think anybody wants to see that again because that was just ugly. I don't want to do that again because that was just some B.S.”

The Eagles on Wednesday also opened the practice windows for rookie tight end Eli Stowers (hamstring), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back) and cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee). They also signed safety Dean Clark to the practice squad. Clark played in 12 games with two starts with the Jets last year.

text:
Story by

Rico Dowdle injury updates: Latest status on Steelers RB foot injury

Running back Jaylen Warren enters NFL Week 6 ranked third in the NFL in scrimmage yards with 640.

The Pittsburgh Steelers would probably prefer for him not to be quite so prolific so early in the year.

REQUIRED READING: Steelers PFF grades: Jaylen Warren's stats surging in Mike McCarthy offense

The heavy workload that created that total has been a necessity because of the absence of Rico Dowdle, the veteran signed by GM Omar Khan this offseason to bolster the team's depth at the position.

1 / 12

How have Pittsburgh Steelers head coaches fared through the years?

Rico Dowdle injury update

Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of a foot injury sustained against the New England Patriots, which included dislocating the same toe twice.

"Rico is — he's been injured, but he looked good [Oct. 9 and 10]," McCarthy said in his weekly news conference Oct. 13. "He's definitely close to getting back there."

Dowdle was back on the practice field Wednesday in a limited capacity as the team geared up for the Week 6 matchup against the Tampa Bay Bucanneers.

Pittsburgh Steelers running back depth chart

Jaylen Warren

Rico Dowdle

Warren has handled the vast majority of carries in his place. Over the past three weeks, he's taken 49 of the team's 64 touches.

To his credit, the production has been phenomenal. He had 194 yards from scrimmage in Week 3 against the Bengals; 126 in the Week 4 loss at Cleveland; and 188 in the Week 5 win against the Colts.

The latter effort included an 80-yard touchdown catch and 50-yard touchdown run. It was the first such combo of explosive plays in the NFL since Herschel Walker completed it in 1986.

Once Dowdle is back, McCarthy left little doubt about who will lead the backfield.

"Jaylen is our featured player right now," he said. "I mean, let's make sure we all recognize that. He's hot. He's playing great football for us. So, it's important for us, as an offense, coaches and players alike, to continue to put him in position to make plays. So that won't change."

Nevertheless, expect Dowdle to still have a significant role. The Steelers did not sign him to a two-year, $12.25 million contract to ride the bench. He's been a 1,000-yard back each of the past two seasons. He was with McCarthy in Dallas in 2024 before having a nice year separately with Carolina in 2025.

There's also a need to be careful with Warren's usage. At present, he's on pace for a career high in carries, and that includes the first two weeks when he touched the ball less often. He's simultaneously on pace for a career high in receptions as well.

A 60-40 split in Warren's favor seems like a fair expectation, with flexibility to lean harder on Warren as matchups and situations dictate built into McCarthy's gameplan.

text:
The rib injury that sidelined Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. for overtime of a "Sunday Night Football" defeat to the Baltimore Ravens last week isn't expected to keep him out of this week's game against the Chicago Bears.

Although the injury was likely going to limit Penix in practice on Wednesday, the third-year pro is on track to start Sunday at home versus the 3-2 Bears, Kevin Stefanski told reporters.

When asked directly if Penix will start the Week 6 matchup, Stefanski said, "Yes."

"As long as everything goes according to plan," the first-year Falcons head coach qualified.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season

Injuries have been a thorn in Penix's side throughout his football life — long before he even reached the league, too.

He missed the first two contests of the season while working his way back to game action from a partially torn ACL that required season-ending surgery last year. That setback marked the 26-year-old's fifth season-ending injury in the span of eight seasons between his college and NFL careers.

In his absences this season, the 2-3 Falcons have turned to a collection of different signal-callers. Atlanta was going to start former Miami Dolphins QB1 Tua Tagovailoa in its season opener at Pittsburgh; however, Tagovailoa sustained an oblique injury in practice leading up to that game. He was ruled out, and veteran backup Cooper Rush started in his place.

Rush, though, dealt with back spasms prior to that start and threw two interceptions, including a fourth-quarter pick-6, in a one-score defeat. Rush was tabbed the starter for Week 2 as well, but he was replaced by undrafted rookie and former Division II standout Jack Strand in a blowout loss to the Carolina Panthers.

Penix's return the following week sparked Atlanta's early-season turnaround. The Falcons bounced back from an 0-2 start with back-to-back victories. They authored a pair of statement-making wins on the road, combining for 80 points while taking down the Green Bay Packers and the New Orleans Saints. Along the way, Penix completed 73.3% of his attempts and passed for 479 yards, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception.

While his completion rate dipped versus the Ravens last time out, he threw for 240 yards and a touchdown in a game the Falcons led 23-15 late in the fourth quarter.

After Baltimore's Tyler "Snoop" Huntley orchestrated a game-tying drive, Penix went down with his rib injury on a sack. After missing a play, he returned for one in the final moments of regulation. Except when overtime began, he was held out.

Following a seven-plus-minute Ravens touchdown drive, Tagovailoa tossed a game-ending interception.

Stefanski explained Wednesday that he and his coaching staff would dictate Penix's rep count by taking the temperature on how the 2024 No. 8 overall pick was feeling in practice.

"With any injury like this, you want to make sure as they move around and how they're feeling — it could be all, some, none," Stefanski said, regarding the reps the Falcons could potentially take off Penix's plate that day. "We shall see."

Penix reportedly had imaging done earlier this week. Stefanski didn't divulge specifics concerning the extent of the rib issue his quarterback is navigating.

Stefanski did note, though, that Penix is "feeling better."

Atlanta is gearing up to face a Bears squad that could get Caleb Williams back this week. Williams has been out since his scary Grade 2 hamstring injury late in a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

"I think you got to prepare for everybody on the roster," Stefanski said Wednesday. "Obviously, Caleb Williams is tremendous and so talented and can make every single throw, can play on time, can play off schedule. He's a very, very, very good young quarterback and has the stats and the wins to back that up."

Stefanski added, alluding to backups Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum: "They also have two guys that have started and won for them. So I think you have to prepare for the entire roster and understand of course there's differences in play style, but we have to make sure we prepare for the entire roster."

text:
If you’re like me, you watched the end of Ravens-Falcons on Sunday night with an overwhelming sense of dread. The moment Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. pulled that towel over his head on the sideline as the Ravens rolled in overtime, I knew the game was over. And I was very worried about Penix’s availability in the short term.

Thankfully, Penix was able to practice fully on Wednesday. After practice, he noted that he made all of his throws on Wednesday.

“They get better every day. I felt good today at practice,” Penix said. “… I just gotta stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I’m doing all the right things.”

Penix would not elaborate on the nature of the injury (he was asked if it’s a bruised rib, and he said he didn’t want to get too specific). But he did tell us the MRI was positive. Thankfully, before I got a chance to, Marc Raimondi from ESPN clarified with Penix that the MRI was not positive for any type of injury, but the results of the MRI were positive for Penix’s chances to start agains the Bears on Sunday.

“Positive means I’m good to play,” said Penix.

Even though Penix felt good in practice, it wasn’t perfect.

“It’s not always comfortable, but I made every throw today,” he said.

During the limited portion of practice we are permitted to watch, Penix was definitely moving around well today. There wasn’t any noticeable hesitation or gingerness in his rib area as he worked through drills.

One little bit of luck for Atlanta is the absence of Montez Sweat this week due to his suspension for violating the league’s PED policy. But Penix, while acknowledging the mark Sweat can leave on games, said that the rest of the defensive front in Chicago is also tough.

“I feel like he is an impact player, so he makes impacts on games, but the next-man-up mentality in the league — I feel like the guys that’s right behind are almost as good. They’re very close. So it’s hard for us to try to say that that’s going to change much because of him being out.”

We’ll see what the official injury report says about Penix when it’s released Wednesday, and we’ll continue to monitor his status through the week and heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bears.

title: Bears to make Caleb Williams a full participant in Wednesday's injury report - Chicago Sun-Times
description:
But the Bears’ decision to call Caleb Williams a full participant in Wednesday’s estimated injury report has opened up a lane that could end with him starting Sunday’s game in Atlanta.
The Bears would have to average 40.6 points the rest of the season to surpass the 2013 Broncos’ 606 points.
“It’s getting back to what we did all through [training] camp and how we started the first week of the season,” Johnson said.
Being a full participant, even on an estimated injury report, was an important step Wednesday.

text:
Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters Wednesday he plans to start quarterback Michael Penix, who has injured ribs, “as long as everything goes accordingly.”

Bears coach Ben Johnson wasn’t that blunt — he rarely is, when it comes to his quarterback situation. But the Bears’ decision to call Caleb Williams a full participant in Wednesday’s estimated injury report has opened up a lane that could end with him starting Sunday’s game in Atlanta.

Johnson wouldn’t name a starter Wednesday, though. He wouldn’t even elaborate on the pecking order at quarterback. That’s a steep fall from where Johnson had stood at different points earlier in the young season.

The coach who spoke openly about trying to score more points than any team in the history of the NFL actually looked like he could after posting 59 points in the season opener against the Panthers. Johnson’s offense has since scored 12 points or fewer in three of his last four games. The Bears would have to average 40.6 points the rest of the season to surpass the 2013 Broncos’ 606 points. It’s not going to happen.

Williams played maybe the best game of his career in the opener, finishing with 269 passing yards a 124.1 passer rating. To become the first Bears passer to throw for 4,000 yards, though, he’d have to start every game the rest of the season and average 300 yards per game. That’s unlikely to happen, either.

The lofty goals set at the beginning of the season have been simplified. The Bears need a win against the Falcons — whose quarterback, Penix, was a full practice participant — before playing last year’s Super Bowl participants in the ensuing two weeks.

“It’s getting back to what we did all through [training] camp and how we started the first week of the season,” Johnson said. “I don’t know that we’ve done that at a consistent level since then.”

Johnson not being willing to list his quarterback depth chart is a testament to the debacle of the past week.

Just two-and-a-half weeks ago, third-stringer Keenum was sharp against the Eagles — and charmed America — on “Monday Night Football.” Fans driving home from Soldier Field that night undoubtedly believed that Johnson could turn even a third-string quarterback into a prime-time player. Johnson then switched to Tyson Bagent as the starter. He dodged calamity against the Jets — three interceptions came back because of a penalty — but was solid in a 23-12 win against the Jets. That earned him a repeat role as starter Sunday in Green Bay, where he was a disaster. Keenum came on in relief after Bagent threw his second interception. Neither fared well, though Keenum was put in scramble mode because the Bears were down 24 points when he entered the game.

“I put our struggles on myself more than anything else from the game the other day,” Johnson said. “I have to do a better job making sure we get in a rhythm on offense, regardless of who’s playing the quarterback position.”

Johnson still isn’t willing to state his preference between Bagent and Keenum.

“A lot of things have gone through our minds,” Johnson said. “First and foremost, health is the No. 1 priority for all three guys. I don’t know that any of them are exactly 100% at this point in the season. That’s something that we certainly look at. We want whoever is out there to have a good rapport with the offensive line, with the operation, with our pass catchers. So, we want to make sure that we can get in a rhythm, which we weren’t able to do last week as an offense. So, sure. It all goes into account here. What do we need to do first and foremost for this week? And then a big-picture view.”

The offense’s struggles have varied by the game. Johnson rattled off red zone concerns, three-and-outs and, last week, turnovers as reasons for concern.

“Our play style needs to show up on a regular basis,” he said.

Williams hurt his right hamstring while trying to run into the end zone in the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss to the Vikings. He returned to practice Friday, where he was a limited participant, and was put through a workout at Lambeau Field hours before kickoff. Being a full participant, even on an estimated injury report, was an important step Wednesday. The Bears held a walk-through, something Johnson claimed was planned weeks in advance to help the Bears prepare for the quick turnaround. That meant the team merely had to submit an estimated injury report to the league.

Complicating matters about his return is the fact the Bears play two games in five days — Sunday and the following Thursday against the Patriots at Soldier Field. If

Williams plays Sunday, he’d have to be prepared to rebound physically.

text:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga, who left Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Chargers with an ankle injury, is expected to miss multiple weeks, sources told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Wednesday.

Hufanga did not practice in the shortened week leading up to the Broncos' Thursday night game against the Seattle Seahawks. One source estimated that Hufanga could miss two to three weeks, depending on how he recovers. That could push Hufanga's absence through the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

Hufanga's impact on the Broncos defense has been especially evident over the past three weeks. In the win over the Los Angeles Rams to close out September, Hufanga became just the fifth safety in NFL history to have two interceptions, an interception return for a touchdown and a sack in the same game.

In the first quarter of Sunday's win over the Chargers, he forced a fumble on Chargers tight end Charlie Kolar and recovered the ball. It led to the Broncos' first touchdown of the game four plays later.

"[Turnovers] are purposeful," Broncos coach Sean Payton said Tuesday. "It happened with [Hufanga] early in the game. ... Those are huge, huge swings of momentum."

Hufanga was injured with 2 minutes, 50 seconds left in the third quarter when he tackled, with defensive tackle D.J. Jones, Chargers running back Omarion Hampton for a 2-yard loss. Hufanga did not return to the game and did not participate in the team's on-field work this week.

He is fourth on the team in tackles with 23. Devon Key, who was a first-team All Pro selection as a special-teamer last season, has played in Hufanga's safety spot alongside Brandon Jones and is expected to start Thursday against the Seahawks.

FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez, who has missed the past two games due to a shoulder injury, said he will return for Sunday's home game against the New York Jets.

"I'm good now, ready for Sunday," Gonzalez told reporters Wednesday.

Gonzalez injured his shoulder in the team's Week 3 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and initially thought he was OK after the game. He explained Wednesday what unfolded in the days following the game.

"At that point, you got a lot of adrenaline. Adrenaline covers a lot of things in this sport," he said. "At that time, I felt good. Things happen, so it is what it is and I'm ready for this week.

"... I've been itching, kind of going a little crazy when I'm not getting to play. It's hard. You put in work with all these guys and then you don't get to be out there with them."

Gonzalez watched the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday from the sideline, saying it was important to him to be there for his teammates.

In addition to Gonzalez's return, receiver A.J. Brown is returning to practice for the first time since being placed on injured reserve Sept. 12, according to coach Mike Vrabel. This is the first day Brown is eligible to return and Vrabel said he would "see how that goes" before determining if Brown plays Sunday.

Players were buoyed by news of Brown's return to practice.

"Huge boost. He's a receiver one," veteran safety Kevin Byard said. "Obviously the past couple weeks our pass game has been playing really well so he adds another dynamic to that."

text:
After their quarterback couldn't finish Sunday night's overtime loss to the Baltimore Ravens due to a rib injury, the Atlanta Falcons are getting some positive news relating to Michael Penix Jr.'s status for Week 6. On Wednesday, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Penix is "feeling better" and that, if "everything goes according to plan," he will start on Sunday against the Chicago Bears.

"Mike will practice," Stefanski said to begin his Wednesday press conference. "He'll be limited in some fashion. We'll see how he's feeling and have communication with him to see how many reps we'll take off, so that's to be determined."

When asked specifically if Penix will start on Sunday, Stefeanski said, "Yes, as long as everything goes according to plan."

Stefanski went on to say that he wants to see how Penix is feeling out on the field before making hard determinations on how the practice reps will be divvied up.

"With any injury like this, you want to make sure, as they move around, how they're feeling," he said. "It could be all, some, none. We shall see."

Penix suffered the injury after being sacked by Baltimore's Tavius Robinson with about 19 seconds left in regulation. He fumbled the ball after getting hit, but the Falcons recovered the football. Penix was forced to miss that next play, but did return one play later, throwing an incompletion before Atlanta punted the ball away. The game eventually went to overtime.

Despite that brief return, the former first-round pick did not go back onto the field during the overtime period, as Tua Tagovailoa relieved him the rest of the way. After the Ravens scored a touchdown on their opening possession, Tagovailoa tossed a game-clinching interception, with Atlanta falling 30-23.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers continued stacking up wins on Sunday, this time beating the Seattle Seahawks 32-29 in a thriller that went down to the final possession.

Playing banged up offensively, the 49ers capitalized on Seattle’s mistakes in a seven-turnover game, as they improved to 5-0 and remained unbeaten atop the NFC West.

While the 49ers remained unbeaten, the Rams and Seahawks both lost, widening San Francisco’s lead in the NFC West heading into Week 6. With the changes in the NFL this past week, let’s take a look at the industry’s power rankings for Week 6.

ESPN: No. 1

“Under new coordinator Raheem Morris, the Niners rank fifth in yards per play allowed (4.7) and have limited big plays as well as any team in the league,” ESPN’s Nick Wagoner wrote. “But they have struggled to get off the field consistently. The Niners rank 20th in third-down defense, giving up a first down on 40.8% of their opportunities. As a result, their defense has been on the field for 31 minutes, 12 seconds per game, which ranks 23rd in the NFL.”

Rest of top five: Chiefs, Bills, Seahawks, and Jaguars.

The 49ers’ biggest area for improvement is their third-down defense, which ranks 20th in the NFL. Still, despite all their injuries, the 49ers have found ways to keep winning.

NFL.com: No. 1

San Francisco remained No. 1 on NFL.com’s power rankings of the week, and NFL.com’s Nick Shook also pointed out the defense, but in a more positive light.

“There’s something special cooking within San Francisco’s defense, a unit that has every excuse to be average, at best, but continues to exceed expectations,” Shook wrote. “While the final score (32-29) doesn’t suggest it, Sunday’s win in Seattle was a defense-driven victory -- and a big one for the team’s confidence as a true Super Bowl contender.”

Rest of top five: Chiefs, Seahawks, Ravens, and Jaguars.

There seems to be a consensus on the Chiefs, who are also undefeated and coming off their bye week. Meanwhile, most remain extremely high on the Seahawks, which only further validates the 49ers’ win on Sunday.

The Athletic: No. 1

Just like the two above, the 49ers are the top team in The Athletic’s weekly power rankings, with their resume standing out through five games.

“No team has a better resume than the 49ers, who overcame a rare so-so game from Brock Purdy in Seattle,” The Athletic’s Chad Graff and Josh Kendall said. “This time, it was San Francisco’s defense that led the way, limiting the Seahawks to just 4.2 yards per play. Oh, and Mike Evans and George Kittle certainly do not look like they are 33 years old.”

It’s a good sign that the 49ers are winning in different ways, especially considering the gauntlet of a schedule they face to end the season.

Rounding out the top five were the Chiefs, Bills, Vikings, and Jaguars. Despite being one of three undefeated teams, the Vikings haven’t received much love in the power rankings ahead of Week 6, but they did here.

Sports Illustrated: No. 1

The 49ers jumped from No. 5 last week to No. 1 in Connor Orr’s latest power rankings.

“The 49ers lead the league in wins…and players who are on injured reserve,” Orr wrote. “I heard a theory on Monday while making calls that stuck with me: the teams that are at the biggest advantage in the NFL are the ones with continuity at head coach, playcaller and quarterback over a multi-year period, especially during a season in which 10 head coaching jobs shifted this offseason. The steadiness of the Shanahan-Purdy partnership is shining.”

Rounding out the top five were the Jaguars, Chiefs, Bills, and Seahawks.

CBS Sports: No. 1

The 49ers remained atop Pete Prisco’s weekly power rankings for CBS Sports, and he believes this could be their year to win a Super Bowl.

”San Francisco 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan hasn’t won a Super Bowl. That doesn’t mean he isn’t a great coach,” Prisco wrote. “If last season, in which he won 12 games with an injury-ravaged team, didn’t prove how good he is at leading the 49ers, this year is doing just that. The 49ers are 5-0 after going to Seattle and beating the Seahawks on Sunday, doing it with a defense leading the charge, rather than the Shanahan-led offense.

“The 49ers limited the Seattle running attack, forced four turnovers, one of which was recovered in the end zone for a touchdown, and had five sacks, the most they’ve had in a game since 2024. They did it without star pass rusher Nick Bosa. First-year defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is using a much more aggressive scheme than past Shanahan coordinators, and it’s showing up in takeaways and sacks. The coverage is tighter. There are reportedly multiple teams interested in free agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill as he continues to rehab from the knee injury that ended his 2025 campaign.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday that Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said he is still talking with multiple teams even though "nothing is imminent at this time. He's continuing his rehab with the goal of being on a team in the immediate future."

Earlier this month, Michael Silver of The Athletic reported the Kansas City Chiefs were "very interested" in a reunion with Hill, which would make sense.

After all, there is already chemistry with quarterback Patrick Mahomes after Hill played for the AFC West team from 2016 through 2021. He helped the Chiefs win the Super Bowl during the 2019 campaign and was one of the best receivers in the league during that span.

What's more, Kansas City needs wide receiver depth with Tyquan Thornton (ankle) and Rashee Rice (hamstring) dealing with injuries.

Silver also reported Hill was "targeting a November return" from the significant knee injury he suffered that included a dislocation and torn ACL.

That multiple teams would be interested in a 32-year-old coming off such a serious injury is a testament to his past production. Hill's resume includes five First-Team All-Pro selections, eight Pro Bowl nods, six seasons with more than 1,100 receiving yards and three seasons with double-digit touchdown catches.

He led the league in receiving yards (1,799) and touchdown catches (13) during the 2023 campaign with the Miami Dolphins.

Still, he failed to reach the 1,000-yard mark in 2024 and played just four games in 2025 because of the injury. There are plenty of question marks surrounding him, including whether he will still be the same playmaker if his speed is impacted by his age and recovery.

title: Micah Parsons not rushing return to prevent different injury - ESPN

text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers star edge rusher Micah Parsons won't play Sunday against his former team, the Dallas Cowboys, but he said on his podcast that if this was Super Bowl week, he would play.

Parsons has not yet returned to practice since last season's torn ACL and meniscus and remains on the physically unable to perform list.

"The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?'" Parsons said on the latest episode of podcast, "The Edge with Micah Parsons," released this week.

"If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side."

Parsons said he wants to make sure everything is right before he gets back on the field.

"It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin [is] bothering me," he said.

Earlier in the week, Packers coach Matt LaFleur said they're still waiting for Parsons to be medically cleared.

"He's a physical specimen, he's a creature of nature for sure and sometimes you've got to make sure that your body is, I guess, what's the word I'm looking for? Everything is just [in sync]," LaFleur said. "You don't want one leg to be that much stronger than the other leg is what I'm getting at."

Parsons was injured on Dec. 14 and had surgery on Dec. 29. The Packers typically hold out players coming back from ACL surgery for at least nine months. Parsons is about 9½ months removed from surgery.

Parsons had said during training camp this summer that he thought a return against his former team in Week 6 was "very realistic."

"So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on his podcast. "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it."

text:
Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons remains in rehab mode despite being eligible to practice and return to action. The pass rusher won’t play in Sunday night’s showdown against his former team, the Dallas Cowboys.

For Parsons, the timeline was never about when he was eligible to return; it was about when his knee and body told him he could play full-bore without worrying about re-injury to the knee or elsewhere.

“The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?’” he said this week on "The Edge with Micah Parsons” podcast. "If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first.”

Parsons underscored that the main concern isn’t injuring the repaired ACL again, but rather all the things that could go wrong by pushing to return early.

“What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL,” he said. “It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain, right? And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side. ... Throughout just this year, we’ve seen injuries across the league, coming off ACL or coming off injuries where it was like a soft tissue injury, a core muscle injury, ankle injury, so they were just like, 'We’re just gonna make sure everything is right before [you return].' Because everyone knows, it's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks, and then next thing you know, my groin bothering me, now I have a core muscle [injury], now I’m missing [time]?

"It’s about making sure we do everything right.”

We often see players push to return early, only to suffer another injury or three. Some never fully get back to form until the year following the year back.

Yes, some players, particularly at positions that require less explosiveness or cutting to thrive, can come back early, but it’s not the norm. Every body is different and reacts in its own way.

During the offseason, when Parsons underscored that he wouldn’t be ready to start the season, many assumed he would be back for the Week 6 tilt against the Cowboys, his former club, from which he’d forced a trade after contract talks went sour.

Parsons said any rivalry he might have with Jerry Jones’ club takes a back seat to his health.

“So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was,” he said. “It's just another Sunday Night Football game against two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna wanna be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just wanna be healthy again. That's it.

"I don’t care about the team I left or the team they think I want my revenge against. I don’t need revenge. I just need two healthy knees to do what I love to do.”

Parsons has said all offseason that he values being fully healthy at the back end of the season over being semi-healthy for an early return. He and the Packers are sticking to that timeline.

title: Steelers-Buccaneers: Top Storylines & Key Matchups in Week Six
description:
The 1-4 Buccaneers will seek to get some season momentum going after their rousing prime-time win in Dallas on Thursday night.
The emergence of a more effective pass rush could solidify Tampa Bay's spot in the top 10 of the defensive ratings.
Last Thursday in Dallas marked the first game this season in which Tampa Bay scored more points off takeaways than they allowed.
It was also the first game of the season without a turnover by the Bucs' offense.
