text:
In Week Six, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will try to turn their first win of the 2026 season into the start of the streak and get their first victory at home against the visiting Pittsburgh Steelers, who are off to a 3-2 start in a very competitive AFC North. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, with CBS handling the local broadcast.

The 1-4 Buccaneers will seek to get some season momentum going after their rousing prime-time win in Dallas on Thursday night. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who got his first NFL win in his second career start in Week Five, is expected to start for a third straight week though Baker Mayfield is battling hard to return as soon as possible from his right thumb injury. The Bucs definitely found some much-needed offensive momentum in Dallas, racking up 419 yards with a formula of a heavy dose of the ground game (241 yards) and mistake-free passing from Daniels. Tampa Bay's defense was already showing signs of being one of the better units in the league before going into Dallas and holding a Cowboys team that had been averaging 30.5 points per game to just 16. Though the pass rush is still trying to get on track – no sacks in the past two games combined – the Bucs did generate a season-high three takeaways against the Cowboys (more on that below).

The 3-2 Steelers have alternated wins and losses through the first five weeks, most recently pulling away from the Colts in the second half in Week Five to secure a 34-22 win. Aaron Rodgers, playing in his age 42 season, hit the Colts with a trio of touchdown passes and became the first Steelers quarterback since Terry Bradshaw to record three straight games in which he threw three touchdown passes. As Bucky Irving did for Daniels in Dallas, Jaylen Warren supported Rodgers with an explosive performance, recording 188 yards from scrimmage, which included an 80-yard touchdown catch and a 50-yard touchdown run. The Steelers' defense continues to be strong up front with edge rushers T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith combining for 7.5 sacks, and Watt also has one of the team's four interceptions, which he returned for a touchdown. The Steelers are looking to keep pace in the NFC North, in which all four teams are at least 3-2 and the Ravens are in the lead at 4-1.

Here are four major storylines as well as four head-to-head player battles to keep an eye on as the Bucs and Steelers go head to head on Sunday afternoon:

TOP STORYLINES

One More Start for Daniels – Mayfield's injury was a dislocation of the thumb on his throwing hand, which happened near the very end of the Bucs' Week Three loss to Minnesota. The following day, Head Coach Todd Bowles said the gritty quarterback would probably miss "a minimum of three weeks," which would have sidelined him against the Packers, Cowboys and Steelers. He has now missed two games, and while reports have suggested that Mayfield is trying very hard to shorten that initial timeline, Bowles said last Friday that, "Right now, we plan on starting Jalon against the Steelers." Daniels has started the last two games and showed significant improvement from the first one to the second one, completing 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards a touchdown and, most importantly, no interceptions in Dallas. Given his pedigree as an undrafted rookie – the first one ever to start a game at quarterback for the Buccaneers – Daniels has been impressive, but no matter how well he plays the Buccaneers are sure to go back to Mayfield when he is healthy enough to play. It's a possibility that Mayfield will sit out one more game, as originally planned, then return to action in Week Seven at Carolina for a critical game against a division rival. If that's the eventual outcome, that means Daniels has one more opportunity on Sunday against Pittsburgh to go wire to wire and show off what he can do with his strong right arm, his excellent mobility and his surprising poise for such an inexperienced player. The Buccaneers are excited about his future and are seeing signs that it is a bright one.

One More Game Against Rodgers – In the meantime, the Buccaneers will face Aaron Rodgers for what is almost certainly the last time, as the Hall of Fame-bound passer has declared that this will be his 18th and final season. Rodgers has certainly demonstrated that he still has the talent, pinpoint precision and cerebral command that have made him one of the NFL's all-time leaders in virtually every passing category, this season, throwing for 1,234 yards, 10 touchdowns and four interceptions. For the Buccaneers, Sunday's game is an opportunity to conclude their all-time rivalry with Rodgers with a winning record, something only currently five teams can claim (Buffalo, Green Bay, Indianapolis, Pittsburgh and Washington). That ledger currently stands at 3-3, with the Bucs getting the upper hand in games played in 2008, 2009 and 2020, all during Rodgers' tenure in Green Bay, and Rodgers winning in contests staged in 2011, 2014 and 2022. This is the first time that Tampa Bay will face Rodgers in a game since he left Green Bay in 2023, first spending two seasons with the Jets and now two in Pittsburgh. If postseason games are included, then the Buccaneers are trying to protect a head-to-head lead against Rodgers, as the Buccaneers also won in Green Bay in the 2020 NFC Championship Game to punch their ticket to Super Bowl LV.

Whose Defense is For Real? – The Buccaneers and Steelers are both known for having long stretches of defensive dominance during their best eras, and both have produced multiple Hall of Famers on that side of the ball. Defense is in their DNA for both franchises and both are getting strong performances on that side of the ball again in 2026. The Buccaneers have quietly landed in the NFL's top 10 in a wide variety of categories, including net yards allowed, rushing yards allowed, interceptions, first downs allowed and third-down success rate allowed. After giving up 33 points in the season opener in Cincinnati (with seven of those coming on a Bengals defensive score), they have gradually reduced that to 23, 23, 17 and 16 in the last four games. The Buccaneers' efforts have been led by a secondary that is clamping down on some of the NFL's top wideouts, such as Ja'Marr Chase, Christian Watson and, most recently, CeeDee Lamb. They have done so without the complementary help of a robust pass rush, as the Bucs have produced only six sacks through five games. The emergence of a more effective pass rush could solidify Tampa Bay's spot in the top 10 of the defensive ratings. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh's pass rush has been the best aspect of its defensive performance, which is not surprising for a team that employs T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith and Nick Herbig. Watt and Highsmith alone have produced 7.5 sacks, 1.5 more than the Buccaneers as a team. Pittsburgh's defensive ranking in such categories as yards, rushing yards, passing yards and yards allowed per play are more middle of the pack so far, but it is Pittsburgh, not Tampa Bay that ranks in the top 10 in the most important category: points allowed. Which proud defensive organization will have the stronger game on Sunday at Raymond James Stadium?

Turnovers – Do They Really Come in Bunches? – Todd Bowles has often employed the expression that "turnovers come in bunches in the NFL," with his experience telling him that his team will sometimes force a lot of them in a certain stretches of games and sometimes go through droughts where they seem impossible to come by. Bowles' defenses have generally beenquite good at producing takeaways and the offensive havoc they cause; from 2019, when he first arrived as Tampa Bay's defensive coordinator, through last season, the Buccaneers ranked seventh in the league in takeaways. And that production was definitely streaky. Last year, for instance, the Bucs only had two takeaways through the first four games of the season but then racked up 14 over their next six outings. Bowles' crew would like to see a similar trend this year, as they created just two takeaways through their first three games and three quarters but have since racked up five in their last five quarters of play. Last Thursday in Dallas marked the first game this season in which Tampa Bay scored more points off takeaways than they allowed. It was also the first game of the season without a turnover by the Bucs' offense. Will the Bucs get takeaways in bunches in the coming weeks as they try to turn their season around, and can their offense conversely put opposing defenses into a turnover drought?

KEY MATCHUPS

1. Steelers G Brock Hoffman vs. Buccaneers DL Calijah Kancey

After struggling to score points out of the gate this season – the Steelers were last in the NFL in scoring through the first two weeks – the team made some changes up front to try to shore up their front and get better results in the ground game. Rookie Max Iheanachor, a first-round draft pick, replaced Dylan Cook at right tackle and veteran Brock Hoffman, a former Cowboy signed in the offseason for depth. Pittsburgh's offense has improved significantly since then, averaging just under 30 points per game and raising it's per-carry average from 3.4 yards to 4.7. Hoffman had been a part-time starter in Dallas, playing both center and guard, and he has 59 games and 19starts worth of experience. Calijah Kancey will work on either side of the nose tackle so he should see action against all of the Steelers' interior linemen, including Hoffman. Kancey does not have a sack yet in 2026 but he leads Buccaneer defenders in pressures and, according to Next Gen Stats, going into Week Five he had a 12.8% pressure rate that was seventh highest among NFL defensive tackles. Kancey has a very quick first step and that has helped him average 0.85 seconds on his get-off at the snap. Rodgers, of course, is a master at getting rid of the ball quickly enough to avoid pressure, but he has been sacked 14 times already this season, and pressure coming directly up the middle is often the most disruptive kind against any quarterback.

2. Buccaneers T Luke Goedeke vs. Steelers OLB T.J. Watt

The other side of the coin is this pass-rush matchup when Tampa Bay has the football, and it's a critical one for both teams. It's no coincidence that the Bucs got their first win in Week Five in what was also their first game without allowing multiple sacks, but the Cowboys' defense doesn'tfeature an edge rusher of T.J. Watt's caliber. Watt's otherworldly quickness at the snap – he is tied for the fastest get-off of any edge rusher or defensive linemen in the league at 0.71 – makes him a tough draw for any opposing lineman, and since he primarily lines up on the left edge of Pittsburgh's front, that challenge will primarily be presented to Bucs right tackle Luke Goedeke. Goedeke and company had their best showing of 2026 so far in Dallas, as the team ran for 241 yards and Daniels only took one sack and four QB hits. Goedeke is a powerful blocker, and his production is magnified by a nasty, play-to-the-whistle demeanor on the field. Pro Football Focus has Goedeke graded as the 19th best tackle in pass protection this season among 69 candidates. It's hard to completely shut out a pass rusher who has a career rate of 0.85 sacks per game, butkeeping him from wrecking the backfield will be important Sunday. The Steelers' career record when Watt gets two or more sacks in a game is 22-4-1.

3. Cowboys TEs Pat Freiermuth & Darnell Washington vs. Buccaneers LB Josiah Trotter

The production of the Steelers' tight end duo of Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington through five games isn't overwhelming; the two have combined for 30 catches, 300 yards and five touchdowns. However, that belies the fact that Freiermuth and Washington are a critical part of the offense that the Bucs – particularly their linebackers in the middle of the field – need to stop from hurting them. At 6-7 and 264 pounds – which he himself has said is a generously low listing – Washington is perhaps the biggest tight end in the NFL but not a non-factor in the passing game. Freiermuth isn't exactly small, at 6-5 and 258 pounds, meaning the Steelers can trot out a very big lineup to get their run game going. Pittsburgh uses two-TE personnel 24.7% of the time, which is essentially NFL average, but they can always have at least one of their two big tight ends in the mix. Freiermuth is tied for the team lead with 19 receptions and he leads the squad with four touchdown receptions. Washington has 11 catches for 131 yards and one score and is a nightmare for opposing defenders when he gets the ball and starts to pick up steam. Josiah Trotter is off to an impressive start in his rookie campaign, leading the Bucs with 37tackles, the most ever by a Tampa Bay defender through his first four career outings. Trotter's scouting report leading into the draft included questions about his coverage ability, primarily because he wasn't asked to do much in coverage at Missouri, but early returns in that department have been encouraging. After some early-season blips, the Bucs' defense showed improvement in covering tight ends in Dallas, with Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker combining for four catches and 28 yards. Trotter has become a tone-setter for the Bucs' defense already and will be more than happy to do battle with the Steelers' imposing tight ends.

4. Buccaneers RB Bucky Irving vs. Steelers LB Payton Wilson

Bucky Irving's 72-yard run against the Cowboys, in which his multiple changes of direction had Dallas defenders running into each other, was a dazzling example of the elusiveness that made him a breakout star as a rookie in 2024. Irving's second season was marred significantly by injuries and his production and propensity for big plays dipped significantly. The Bucky Irving of 2026 resembles that player from two years ago, not only in the way he stacks sharp cuts but also in his clear joy in being on the field. He finished the game with 175 yards from scrimmage and, for the first time in his career, had a touchdown run and a touchdown catch in the same game. Irving is one of the NFL's best at forcing would-be tacklers to miss, and in Dallas he had career highs in both missed tackles forced (10) and yards gained after missed tackles (122). Irving is also adept in the passing game, something the Bucs haven't leaned on much in recent games but an idea they can always pull out of their bag to try to get their most dynamic player the ball in space. Payton Wilson was a third-round draft pick by the Steelers in 2024 and after opening a total of eight games in his first two seasons he has moved into a full-time starting role in 2026. It has been a productive start for him in that assignment, as he leads the team with 40 tackles and has added a sack, six tackles for loss, two quarterback hits, two passes defensed and a fumble recovery. Wilson has a good size-speed combination at 6-4 and 233 pounds and a 4.43-second 40 time. He is a fluid mover who has sideline-to-sideline range, making him strong in coverage, as well. Wilson and fellow off-ball linebacker Patrick Queen will be looking to keep Irving from having another explosive outing.

text:
New England Patriots left tackle Will Campbell has been diagnosed with an MCL sprain in his right knee and is expected to miss some game action, a source told ESPN on Tuesday.

The initial belief is that Campbell's injury isn't as bad as the Grade 3 torn MCL that he suffered on the same knee last November that led the Patriots to place him on injured reserve. Campbell, the Patriots' first-round pick in 2025, admittedly returned from that injury for the postseason before he was 100% healed and struggled with protecting quarterback Drake Maye.

Rookie first-round pick Caleb Lomu stepped in after Campbell was injured when a Las Vegas Raiders defender tackled running back Rhamondre Stevenson into Campbell's leg on a rushing attempt in the second quarter. Lomu, who played left tackle in college at Utah, is a top candidate to start while Campbell recovers.

"I don't think it was too big for him," Vrabel told reporters of Lomu's fill-in performance. "You didn't really notice him a lot, so I think that's probably a good thing."

With the Patriots tapping their offensive tackle depth, they could benefit from having 2025 seventh-round pick Marcus Bryant -- who was tracking to be the top swing tackle in the preseason -- begin to practice. Bryant had been placed on injured reserve with a designation to return at the final roster cutdown after being rolled up on in a preseason game, and he was eligible to begin practicing last week.

New England has had a difficult run of injuries, losing multiple offensive linemen for the season. Running back TreVeyon Henderson also is expected to miss multiple weeks with a high ankle sprain, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Vrabel said "there's a chance" that receiver A.J. Brown will be activated off injured reserve and can play against the New York Jets on Sunday.

ESPN's Mike Reiss contributed to this report.

title: Philadelphia Eagles guard Brandon Brooks retires from NFL after recent injury-plagued seasons
description:
PHILADELPHIA -- Philadelphia Eagles Pro Bowl right guard Brandon Brooks announced his retirement Wednesday after 10 seasons in the NFL.
Brooks also suffered a season-ending torn pectoral muscle in Week 2 of this past season.
A third-round draft selection of the Texans in 2012, Brooks played his first four seasons in Houston before signing a five-year, $40 million free-agent deal with the Eagles in 2016.
He made three consecutive Pro Bowls from 2017 to '19, and was a key in helping deliver Philadelphia its first Super Bowl title after the 2017 season.
Brooks spent 40 minutes Wednesday expressing his gratitude to former teammates, coaches, and the city of Philadelphia during a videoconference with reporters.
text:
PHILADELPHIA -- Philadelphia Eagles Pro Bowl right guard Brandon Brooks announced his retirement Wednesday after 10 seasons in the NFL.

Brooks, 32, has been hit hard by injuries in recent years. He tore his right Achilles tendon in a 2018 playoff loss to the New Orleans Saints. Brooks made a quick recovery to play every game in 2019 and earn his third Pro Bowl bid, but he suffered a left Achilles tear in the summer of 2020 and missed the entire season.

Brooks also suffered a season-ending torn pectoral muscle in Week 2 of this past season. He said Wednesday that retirement was something he had been contemplating since last offseason.

"After all of these injuries, I just realized, at what point do you listen to your body? I think my body was just telling me I had to make a decision, and I think at this point in time, I think it's the right decision," said Brooks, who plans to stay in the Philadelphia area and apply to business school at the University of Pennsylvania.

A third-round draft selection of the Texans in 2012, Brooks played his first four seasons in Houston before signing a five-year, $40 million free-agent deal with the Eagles in 2016. He made three consecutive Pro Bowls from 2017 to '19, and was a key in helping deliver Philadelphia its first Super Bowl title after the 2017 season.

Brooks' openness about his mental health could prove to be a bigger part of his legacy. He missed multiple games over his career with what was later diagnosed as an anxiety condition and was one of the first NFL players to talk candidly about mental health, helping pave the way to make the issue more mainstream.

"It has always been a part of me, it will always be a part of me. It will always be something that I deal with," he said. "When it comes to that, I just want to be known as a person who was transparent and a person who just wanted to help others by sharing my story."

The Eagles recently had reworked Brooks' contract, possibly in anticipation of Wednesday's announcement, to reduce his 2022 guaranteed salary and create $12.38 million in salary-cap space, a league source told ESPN's Field Yates.

Eagles chairman and CEO Jeffrey Lurie credited Brooks with helping to create and maintain a winning culture in Philadelphia while pointing out his "unique blend of toughness, power, athleticism, intelligence and skill."

"Beyond his on-field accomplishments, I am most proud of the way Brandon represents our organization with exemplary class," Lurie said in a statement. "He is one of the most thoughtful and bravest athletes I have ever been around. Brandon's willingness to openly discuss his own struggles with anxiety has served as an inspiration for so many and helped open the door for future conversations among athletes and role models everywhere. His impact in that area is immeasurable."

Brooks spent 40 minutes Wednesday expressing his gratitude to former teammates, coaches, and the city of Philadelphia during a videoconference with reporters.

"How do you say goodbye to something you've known your whole life?" he said. "Something that taught you triumph, pain, success, failure, perseverance, love, empathy and altruism. I don't know, but I'll try my best."

text:
While so many people in the football world focused on the Patriots' easy strength of schedule in 2025, they overlooked the key to so much of their ability to stack up 14 regular-season wins en route to a Super Bowl appearance: their health.

While they did lose some key players for short stretches, they were able to navigate the season without losing players at positions where they lacked depth.

This year, that luck has turned around significantly. And though they were able to overcome an injury report on Sunday that included four cornerbacks missing the game, they suffered at least two more injuries -- left tackle Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson -- that will further cut into the team's depth. Edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones also suffered a shoulder injury, something he already dealt with earlier in the season. Defensive tackle Cory Durden also suffered a late injury against the Raiders, as did cornerback Charles Woods.

Ever since opening night of the season, when A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener, injuries have been the theme of the season for New England. Right guard Mike Onwenu broke his ankle in Week 3. The team had brought in Greg Van Roten during the summer due to injuries to Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich, but Van Roten suffered a thigh injury in Week 4 that sent him to IR.

Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez has now missed two straight games due to a shoulder injury, while fellow starting corner Carlton Davis has missed two of the Patriots' five games thus far with a neck injury.

A calf injury to Mack Hollins sent the veteran wide receiver to IR, further thinning out the receiver room. At EDGE, veteran Harold Landry remains completely MIA, while rookie Quintayvious Hutchins landed on IR with a knee injury after Week 3. Christian Barmore (shoulder) missed the Buffalo game in Week 4, fullback Reggie Gilliam (ankle) missed Week 5, safety Dell Petus (ankle) landed on IR after Week 2, and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) and rookie tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) both missed Week 3's game.

It's been a lot. But has it been the worst injury luck in the NFL?

According to one source, not quite. Not even close, actually.

Rotowire developed a severity score to rank which teams are the most impacted by injuries. Through the first five weeks of the season, the Patriots rank third, with a severity score of 79.

The San Francisco 49ers are No. 1 in this unfortunate category, and by a wide margin, with a severity score of 99. The Houston Texans are in second, with a score of 84, and there's a big gap behind the Patriots, with the Cardinals and Packers tied for fourth with a score of 67.

The injuries haven't stopped the Niners from starting the year with a perfect 5-0 record, though the Texans are off to a 1-4 start after winning 12 games a year ago. The Patriots are at 3-2, though their loss in Week 1 was much more related to uncharacteristically poor decision-making from Drake Maye than it was to injuries.

The process uses a point system, with an IR placement being five points, a PUP/NFI placement being three points, a game-day injury designation of out or doubtful being two points, and a game-day designation of being questionable being one point.

On the brighter end of the spectrum, the Buccaneers (severity score of 26), Bengals (28), Vikings (34), Bills (35) and Colts (38) are the five healthiest teams thus far.

The Athletic also tried to encapsulate the teams most impacted by injuries this year. Using a different method, The Athletic settled on the Patriots ranking fourth in that category, with the Giants at No. 1, the Niners at No. 2, and the Eagles at No. 3.

As far as relief goes for the Patriots, A.J. Brown is eligible to come off IR as soon as this week. The team will also hope to minimize the damage over the next two games before getting the "mini bye" that will follow their Thursday night matchup in Chicago in Week 7. Their actual bye is on the later end this year, as it comes in Week 11, just before Thanksgiving.

Success in the NFL is found through a combination of a million factors. Smart coaching. Preparation. Offseason training. Film study. Game-day execution. Front-office savvy. A fortunate bounce or two. And plenty of other factors that are within a team's control.

Yet in a sport as violent as football, with car crashes taking place just about every snap, the biggest factor outside of anyone's control is the reality of injuries. And with less than a third of the season finished, the Patriots are going to need a major change of fortune with injuries if they hope to still be standing by season's end.

text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers right tackle Taylor Moton said Tuesday that he coughed up blood before being diagnosed with multiple blood clots in late June. The ailment sidelined him throughout training camp and preseason, and well into the second month of the regular season.

Moton, the longest tenured nonspecialist in Carolina, participated in his first padded practice of 2026 on Tuesday after the Panthers activated his 21-day practice window on the non-football injury (NFI) list. Moton's early season stand-in, first-round pick Monroe Freeling, worked with a trainer off to the side because of a knee injury.

Following practice, during his first conversation with reporters since OTAs, Moton detailed his illness and the steps he took to get back onto the field. Moton said upon returning from a youth football camp in Lansing, Michigan, he experienced symptoms that would eventually lead to the discovery of multiple blood clots in his right lung.

"I started coughing up blood -- and it was like a lot of it," Moton said. "And I could start feeling it leaking through my chest even -- something like really different. So, after 15-or-something minutes, I was like 'Yeah, I've got to go to the hospital.' Went to the hospital, they were doing CT scans, ultrasounds, trying to find what was going on. And that's when they found a multitude of clots in my right lung. ... So from there, they put me on blood thinners, and other than that I was just working. I just couldn't have contact on the blood thinners cause having contact on blood thinners can lead to like a brain bleed ... but ultimately doing everything I could to just work and simulate football without the contact up until then."

Moton said he felt as if his chest were congested, but he soon realized the discomfort was more than just typical congestion when he started tasting blood in his mouth. Moton said doctors aren't sure what caused the ailment, but the 32-year-old lineman is more concerned about future prevention. He was told staying hydrated is part of that prevention, as well as moving around when he travels.

Moton has traveled with the team only once this year, as he went to Jacksonville, Florida, for the Panthers' training camp joint practice and preseason game against the Jaguars. He has been consulting with a bloodwork specialist to be prepared for the weeks ahead, including Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Eagles in Philadelphia.

Moton said he was grateful to get back to work on the practice field with his teammates. He had to weigh the risk-reward factor of such a move earlier this summer.

"Ultimately, I had to just weigh the pros and cons of getting off the blood thinners, and then being able to play ball and the chance of it happening [again]," Moton said. "The chances [of a recurrence] are relatively low right now, after being on the blood thinners for three months."

Moton's former Panthers teammate, defensive end DJ Wonnum -- who now plays for the Detroit Lions -- dealt with a blood clot during his first year with Carolina in 2024. Moton said he spoke with Wonnum about their situations.

The veteran tackle said he has been off the thinners for a "couple of weeks now." He noted that he had to wait for his blood to regulate before returning to workouts through the bye week.

Moton, who dealt with notably high blood pressure and lightheadedness before receiving blood thinner treatment, said the ordeal has given him a better appreciation for football and life.

"Honestly, it gave me more gratitude for life in general," Moton said.

The Panthers didn't release an official injury report Tuesday, but Moton donned full pads for the workout. With Freeling dealing with a knee injury, Moton's long-awaited return would be welcomed, if not necessary, to add stability to the line and the offense.

He's getting ready as if his regular-season debut will take place this weekend at Lincoln Financial Field.

"I'm going into it preparing to play," Moton said. "But ultimately, whether I do or not, that's not my decision. That's the higher-ups, right? So, I'm just doing everything I can to prepare as if I'm going in playing."

Along with Moton, defensive end Tershawn Wharton (neck) and running back Trevor Etienne (ankle) had their 21-day practice windows opened on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list and injured reserve, respectively. Like Moton, Wharton has been sidelined since the start of training camp. Etienne sustained his injury in the preseason finale in August.

All three players will have three weeks to be added to the 53-man roster. The Panthers have three open spots on their main depth chart after putting nose tackle Cam Jackson (shoulder) on injured reserve Tuesday.

text:
Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will have arthroscopic surgery on his right knee when the team returns from London and will miss at least four games.

The Jaguars (4-1) placed Harrison on injured reserve Tuesday, ruling him out for Sunday's game against Houston (1-4) at Wembley Stadium as well as AFC matchups against Indianapolis, Baltimore and Tennessee. His recovery timetable will be determined by what doctors find during the scope.

Backup Walker Little, who has started 39 games over six seasons with Jacksonville, is expected to replace Harrison in the lineup.

Harrison has started 53 games for the Jaguars since they selected him 27th overall in the 2023 NFL draft. The former Oklahoma standout moved from right tackle to left tackle this season in hopes of improving Jacksonville's run game, which ranks 14th and is up from 20th in 2025.

Harrison injured his knee early in the third quarter of last Sunday's 19-17 victory over Philadelphia at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Harrison spun on the field turf to make a block and twisted his knee when he planted his right leg. He was eventually carted to the locker room and had tests Monday.

“It was a weird play,” coach Liam Coen said. “He was trying to block on the turnback, and it just tweaked on him a little bit.”

It's the first major injury for Jacksonville this season. Coen's team has been one of the healthiest in the league through five games.

Long snapper Ross Matiscik injured his right shoulder against the Eagles, and the Jaguars signed veteran Jacob Bobenmoyer to the practice squad to fill in for him. Bobenmoyer flew to London on Monday. The Jags also promoted safety Kaevon Merriweather to the active roster.

Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is dealing with a rib injury that isn't considered serious, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Monday, offering some relief for a team that watched its starter forced to the sideline during a critical moment Sunday night.

Whether Penix actually suits up for Week 6 against the Bears, though, remains genuinely uncertain.

FANTASY FOOTBALL: QB Rankings: Who To Start Week 6?

Penix was injured on a hit to his rib area late in the fourth quarter of Atlanta's 30-23 overtime loss to Baltimore, forcing him to watch backup Tua Tagovailoa take over for the extra period.

Tagovailoa's night ended with a game-sealing interception, a frustrating coda for a Falcons team that had Penix playing well up to that point.

"Knowing me, I'm going to be ready to go next week because I sat out enough in my career, but I'm going to do everything I can in the training room, make sure I get back to where I want to be," Penix said postgame. He also admitted to being frustrated watching from the sideline as Tagovailoa's drive unraveled.

The team is treating this with real caution given Penix's injury history

Schefter's full report framed the situation clearly: "Michael Penix's rib injury is not considered serious, per sources.

Penix might be able to return for Sunday's game vs. the Bears, but the team wants to be cautious and see him practice this week before it knows whether he will be able to play in Week 6.

That caution isn't arbitrary. Penix only returned this season after tearing his ACL last year, and Atlanta has every incentive to avoid rushing him back.

Falcons coaching staff said they expect to have a clearer picture of Penix's status once the team holds its first full practice of the week. Until then, Atlanta is keeping its options open rather than committing to a starter.

If Penix can't go, Atlanta turns back to its veteran backup

Should Penix be held out, Tagovailoa would get the start against Chicago, a scenario the Falcons would clearly prefer to avoid given how much more dynamic the offense has looked with Penix at the controls this season.

Atlanta sits at 2-3 and can't afford many more results like Sunday's, making this week's practice reports worth watching closely before Sunday's kickoff.

text:
CHICAGO (AP) — Caleb Williams could return for the Chicago Bears as soon this weekend at Atlanta. If Williams is unable to play, well, the next man up is still being worked out at the moment.

Tyson Bagent threw two interceptions during Sunday’s 31-7 loss at Green Bay. Case Keenum was picked off and lost a fumble after replacing Bagent early in the fourth quarter.

The Bears (3-2) had five turnovers against the Packers, matching their total for the first four games of the season combined.

“Like I said before, it’s nothing we can’t fix enough or won’t fix,” offensive lineman Jonah Jackson said Monday. “We’re just getting started. And the cool thing is we’ll be able to see them again.”

Williams is close to returning after missing three games with a right hamstring injury. But coach Ben Johnson was noncommittal when asked who would serve as the No. 1 quarterback if Williams isn’t available for practice on Wednesday.

“No determination has been made in terms of what direction we’re going,” Johnson said. “There are a lot of things that we’re assessing right now.”

Williams hasn’t played since he got hurt in the fourth quarter of a 9-3 loss to Minnesota on Sept. 20. The No. 1 pick in the 2024 draft worked out on the field before the loss to the Packers.

“He’s doing a great job progressing and we’ll see when we can make him available to help us win ballgames,” Johnson said. “But he’s itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we’ll move forward from there.”

Keenum started Chicago’s 27-7 win over Philadelphia on Sept. 28, passing for 247 yards and two touchdowns. But Bagent was in the NFL’s concussion protocol for much of week ahead of the Eagles victory.

Johnson went with Bagent for a 23-12 victory over the New York Jets in Week 4, and he threw for a career-high 268 yards in his most extensive regular-season action since his rookie year in 2023. He also threw an interception and had three more picks wiped out by penalties on New York.

The situation at quarterback has contributed to a bit of a roller-coaster start to the season for Chicago’s offense.

“The things we take a lot of pride in on offense are how we go about our business from a fundamentals, technique and finish standpoint,” Johnson said. “And those things aren’t consistent at the level with which we’d like them to be right now, so as a coaching staff, we got to make sure that we’re crystal clear on what the expectations are and we’ve got to get that out of our guys.”

What’s working

Well, Tory Taylor had a good day in Green Bay. He punted four times for an average of 53 yards, posting his eighth career game with an average of 50-plus yards on a minimum of four punts.

What needs help

Chicago has lost its first two NFC North games for the second straight year. It is 2-6 against its division in the regular season since Johnson was hired as coach.

The Bears managed to win the North last year for the first time since 2018, but their trouble in division play isn’t exactly a promising long-term strategy. Their next division game is Nov. 26 at Detroit.

Stock up

Austin Booker sacked Jordan Love on back-to-back plays on Green Bay’s final drive of the first half. He became the first player with sacks on consecutive plays for the Bears since Lamarr Houston accomplished the feat against the Chargers on Nov. 9, 2015.

The 23-year-old Booker, a fifth-round pick in the 2024 draft, has a team-high four sacks in five games this season. He had a career-high 4 1/2 sacks in 10 games last year.

“When you see the snap count go up, you see the production go up. And I think that’s all there is to it,” Booker said.

Stock down

With Kyle Monangai sidelined by toe and thumb injuries, Roschon Johnson had an opportunity to make a case for an expanded role. The running back had a team-high five receptions for 34 yards, but he finished with just 6 yards on five rushing attempts.

If Monangai remains out, the Bears could take a closer look at Zavier Scott or Salvon Ahmed on their practice squad.

Injuries

Johnson said he didn’t have an update on the team’s injuries in Sunday’s loss. Linebacker T.J. Edwards left with a hamstring injury in the first half. Defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quadriceps) and defensive backs Tyrique Stevenson (hamstring) and Cam Lewis got hurt in the second half.

Key number

5 — In the loss to the Packers, the Bears became the first team to allow five completions of 35-plus yards in a game since the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 2 of the 2019 season against the San Francisco 49ers.

Next steps

Chicago takes on Bijan Robinson and Atlanta on Sunday. It’s the first meeting between the teams since the Bears beat the Falcons 37-17 at Soldier Field on Dec. 31, 2023.

text:
New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson is expected to miss multiple weeks because of a high ankle sprain, league sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Henderson will not need surgery, sources told Schefter, and the Patriots are hoping that the second-year running back returns relatively soon.

Henderson suffered the injury in the second quarter of New England's victory Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders. The injury occurred at the end of an 11-yard run when Henderson was tackled by safety Jeremy Chinn along the sideline and came up hobbling.

Henderson also missed New England's season opener last month because of an ankle injury. He has 163 yards and one touchdown on 42 carries in four games this season.

With Henderson sidelined Sunday, Corey Kiner served as New England's primary backup to starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson. Kiner rushed for 52 yards on six carries but lost a fumble, while Stevenson had 64 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries.

The Patriots (3-2) are likely to elevate Lan Larison from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the New York Jets (2-3) to give them a third option. Larison, who initially joined the team as an undrafted free agent in 2025 out of UC-Davis, played in the 2026 season opener when Henderson was out -- totaling three offensive snaps and contributing two receptions for nine yards, while playing six snaps on special teams.

ESPN's Mike Reiss contributed to this report.

"I think it'll be pretty miraculous for Jalyx to play this week," Fangio said Tuesday in his weekly press conference.

text:
Do you believe in miracles?

It might take one for the Eagles to have one of their best pass rushers on the field Sunday at the Linc against the Panthers in Week 6.

It might take another one for the Birds' depleted edge defender group to generate enough pressure to slow down Carolina's suddenly explosive offense as the Eagles try to snap a three-game losing streak.

Third-year EDGE Jalyx Hunt almost certainly won't dress barring a recovery so speedy it might take divine intervention to happen, according to defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.

"I think it'll be pretty miraculous for Jalyx to play this week," Fangio said Tuesday in his weekly press conference. "But he's the kind of guy, he's going to be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him. He's not going to be one of those guys that's gonna be hesitant to come back."

The second part of that Fangio quote can be seen as encouraging that Hunt won't be out long enough to go on injured reserve. The left knee and ankle injuries he sustained near the end of the first half against the Jags looked gruesome and required assistance to get him to the sideline.

Hunt being down against the Panthers would leave the Eagles with just Nolan Smith Jr., Jonathan Greenard, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa as the edge defender group – and that's assuming Greenard is ready to play after being inactive Sunday against the Jaguars because of an ankle injury.

Greenard has only played 37 snaps this season after missing all of training camp and the first four weeks of the season from a pectoral injury, so he can't be expected to be conditioned enough to play a truckload of snaps, if he does dress.

"Hopefully he'll be ready to go this week," Fangio said, "but we've got to see."

The Eagles are already struggling to generate sacks. They have just six for the season, tied for fourth-fewest in the NFL, and only have two from an edge rusher, both belonging to Smith. The Panthers have the NFL's third-ranked total offense, second-ranked passing offense and fourth-ranked scoring offense.

text:
The New England Patriots added a pair of key players to their growing list of injury concerns during their blowout win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday as running back TreVeyon Henderson and left tackle Will Campbell each exited and did not return.

On Tuesday, NFL insiders provided updates on both Henderson and Campbell's injuries.

Of the pair, the news was worse for Henderson. According to Adam Schefter of ESPN, the running back suffered a high ankle sprain in the second quarter of Sunday's game and is expected to miss multiple weeks.

According to Schefter, Henderson will not require surgery and the team is hoping he will be back "relatively soon."

The news was slightly better for Campbell, whose right knee got rolled up on, also in the second quarter. It was the same knee that Campbell hurt last year. Last season, he was placed on injured reserve. When he returned to action, Campbell wasn't the same player for the stretch run as New England made it all the way to the Super Bowl.

Following Sunday's injury, Tom Pelissero reported that Campbell avoided a major knee injury. The NFL insider reported that Campbell is considered week-to-week.

Rookie first-round draft pick Caleb Lomu would likely replace Campbell at left tackle should he be forced to miss time. Lomu came in following Campbell's injury and performed well against the Raiders.

The Patriots have won back-to-back games despite a growing injury list. Star cornerback Christian Gonzalez missed both games, and fellow defensive back Carlton Davis joined him as inactive against the Raiders.

The team has also been shorthanded at wide receiver. Offseason acquisition A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the team's season opener and hasn't played since, though according to multiple reports he could be nearing a return. In addition, Mack Hollins was placed on injured reserve with a calf injury he suffered against the Bills.

Head coach Mike Vrabel was asked after Sunday's game how the team has embraced the next man up mentality.

"Because that's what it has to be. You know what I mean? It's, we try not to panic," Vrabel said. "We just try to get the next guy ready. We ask everybody to prepare as a starter, so credit to the football players, you know, particularly the guys on this team, uh, the guys that we've tried to bring in here. And they realize that when you get an opportunity and you do something with it, then you get more opportunities."

text:
CINCINNATI -- A key Cincinnati Bengals passing option is likely out for the season.

Tight end Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral in last Sunday's win over the Miami Dolphins, his agent told ESPN on Tuesday. The injury is expected to cause him to miss the remainder of the season.

Hudson, 31, suffered the injury while trying to make a tackle on special teams in Cincinnati's 31-24 road victory on Week 5. Earlier in the game, he had three catches for 14 yards and a touchdown reception, which prompted praise from Bengals coach Zac Taylor.

"He's just Mr. Dependable," Taylor said Sunday. "Whether he's on the practice squad, whether he's on the roster, he's going to show up. He's been who we thought he was."

Taylor revealed the injury on Monday and said the team was gathering more information to determine whether or not Hudson would be placed on injured reserve.

Hudson, an eighth-year player out of Southern Arkansas, was a surprise cut when the team trimmed the roster to 53 players. He was re-signed to the practice squad and elevated for Weeks 1 and 3.

Hudson was signed to the active roster on Sept. 29, when the Bengals placed cornerback Jalen Davis on injured reserve and waived Ke'Shawn Williams, who was later re-signed to the practice squad.

Hudson has spent the past four seasons with the Bengals. In 42 appearances with the club, he has had 84 catches for 707 yards and five touchdowns.

text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been able to survive a lot of injuries this season. While Deebo Samuel was a late addition this offseason, the team missing him for the next couple of weeks is really going to test what the offense can do.

San Francisco 49ers pass catchers must step up after Deebo Samuel injury

As things stand, the 49ers are very top-heavy in their pass-catching corps. The room has 137 total targets. There are four players who make up 107 of those targets. Samuel has 16 receptions for 206 yards this season. Of those, 80 came on a trick play where he did not even make the reception.

So, even as the fourth option, he was not bringing much. Still, he had to be respected as a legitimate option. The offense lost Jake Tonges for the season earlier in the year. Kyle Juszczyk is going to miss the next couple of weeks as well. Even Demarcus Robinson is currently fifth on the team in targets, and he is on the IR.

Without Samuel, the offense is highly reliant on Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, and Mike Evans.

Jacob Cowing has five targets and just one reception. Jordan Watkins has 60 yards on two receptions. Luke Farrell is playing more due to the injuries but is a blocking option who has two receptions for 19 yards.

The 49ers are starting to get too thin in their skill players. McCaffrey, Kittle, and Evans can carry the group, but if all three are being asked to have their best performances throughout the season, the sustainability of this success is not going to last.

Evans has already missed time this year, Kittle is coming back from an injury, and McCaffrey has a few serious injuries on his resume as well.

Because Juszczyk, Robinson, and Samuel will be back at some point, the assumption is the 49ers will not make a drastic move to add a playmaker. Still, it will be tough to get by until then, and the team could end up looking into a trade option as some teams begin to understand they are sellers this year.

The 49ers built up a 5-0 record, and they beat the defending Super Bowl champions. However, that does not guarantee the team is going to win anything in the postseason. They still have to preserve their roster and ensure they can make a run.

text:
Overshown has dealt with several injuries over the course of his NFL career, beginning in 2023 with a torn ACL in his left knee and a torn ACL, MCL and PCL in his right knee in the 2024. This injury is not as severe for Overshown, but is still a frustrating one. When asked about it, Overshown split up his answers into two separate viewpoints.

"For DeMarvion Overshown, it's hard," Overshown said. "As a man, as a father, as a son, you want to do whatever you can to make your family happy. You want to be out on the field. You know how much you sacrifice all year, all offseason just to play healthy, especially being in my shoes. It's hard for me…"

"Agent 0, the Cowboys linebacker, bump and roll. I've been here before. I have all my faith in God, His plan and His plan. So who am I to question? Whether it was getting hurt the first game, getting hurt the 10th game, you never want it to happen. If it's in His will, I'm going to let it be done and I'm just gonna continue to work every day. I want to play. I want to be out there, but it's football, I've got to take my body, take care of myself."

Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Overshown's status for Sunday night against Green Bay is still TBD.

Five games into the year, the Cowboys sit at 2-3 and have allowed the second-most total yards per game in the NFL this season (395.4). On Monday morning, Overshown said the Cowboys defense had a "heart to heart" meeting as they look to turn the corner.

"Looking ourselves in the mirror," Overshown said of what was discussed in the meeting. "Putting what we wanted our standard to be, we put that on the board. We went by bullet point, bullet point. Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it? Just hearing from all of us. It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation, it was more so, 'What can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays, or every Monday walk throughs?' We've got to talk to each other like that because the ship is only going to go as far as the weakest person on the boat. As long as we all in this together, I think we're going to be great. I know we're going to be there."

In Overshown's eyes, the Cowboys have everything necessary to be among the best defensive units in the league.

"It's no reason why we couldn't be a defense that only allowed 10 points a game," Overshown said. "Our thing is not shooting ourselves in the foot, the mental errors. Once we get past that, we're going to be one of the best defenses in the league, we've just got to stop shooting ourselves in the foot."

When he returns, Overshown believes he can be part of the solution for Dallas' struggles to start the season.

"I feel like I'm a pretty good football player," Overshown said. "Getting me back on the field, whether that's [Barham], [Dee Winters], anybody, any other rotation that we're going to have, I feel like it's just going to better our room, which is going to better the defense, which is going to better the team overall. I like to look at myself as one of the guys on this team. When I get back on the field, I can definitely help in some way or some fashion."

In Overshown's absence, rookie Jaishawn Barham has played the MIKE linebacker position and worn the green dot for the Cowboys defense, communicating between DC Christian Parker and the other 10 players on the field. Overshown hasn't been surprised by what Barham has been able to accomplish.

"He's a dog," Overshown said. "I feel like I've been saying that since camp, and we've been saying it since camp. He's a dog. He's getting better every week, he's learning. He's definitely took the green dot role and treated it as a sign of respect, authority, took it as a patch of honor like 'Let me run the show as a rookie.' He's been doing good. I've been trying to do my best however I can help him. He's going to be a player, a great player, for a long time for this team and in the league in general."

One question that remains when Overshown returns is where he'll slot in at linebacker. Overshown was the green dot and MIKE to start the season, but with Barham's play, could he move back to the weakside linebacker position where he's spent most of his career? As of now, the Cowboys staff hasn't told Overshown.

"They haven't communicated that, but I mean, it really don't matter," Overshown said when asked about if Barham would remain as the MIKE and green dot. "We both, the linebacker positions are both the same, and then the green dot is the person that's basically just communicating from CP. So really depending on what they decide to do. But it won't change how we play at all, it'll still be the same stuff."

The Cowboys have their weekly players day off Tuesday, and will return to practice on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday as Overshown hopes to get back in the lineup for Dallas against the Packers.

text:
The Buffalo Bills survived overtime in Los Angeles.

Now they have six days to get ready for another road game with a growing injury list.

Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns.

The Bills already played without wide receiver D.J. Moore, defensive tackle Ed Oliver, cornerback Dee Alford and wide receiver Joshua Palmer against the Rams.

Buffalo also had safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson, linebacker Terrel Bernard and cornerback Christian Benford leave briefly Monday, although all three returned.

The Las Vegas Raiders have their own injury questions entering Week 6, including running back Ashton Jeanty, who played through ankle and foot injuries in Sunday's loss to New England.

Buffalo (4-1) visits Las Vegas (3-2) at 4:25 p.m. ET Sunday, Oct. 18, at Allegiant Stadium. The Bills have their bye in Week 7.

NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation.

A game status report is due by 4 p.m. Friday for Sunday games.

Here is the latest Bills vs. Raiders injury update for Week 6.

Buffalo Bills injury update for Week 6

Spencer Brown, OT, back

Spencer Brown is Buffalo's biggest new injury concern entering Week 6.

Brown left Monday night's game after Josh Allen completed a 6-yard pass to Khalil Shakir with 6:22 remaining in the second quarter.

Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return.

Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter.

Bills coach Joe Brady did not have an update after the game.

Brown has dealt with back issues before. He underwent back surgery prior to the 2022 season and began 2025 training camp on the physically unable to perform list because of a back flare-up.

Tylan Grable replaced Brown and played the final 48 offensive snaps at right tackle. He was flagged for offensive holding and a false start.

C.J. Gardner-Johnson, S, leg

C.J. Gardner-Johnson gave Buffalo a scare Monday night.

Gardner-Johnson was injured while tackling Rams running back Blake Corum after a 34-yard catch-and-run late in the third quarter.

He stayed down after the play and repeatedly pointed toward his leg as Bills athletic trainers came onto the field. Gardner-Johnson eventually got up and limped off under his own power.

He returned for Buffalo's next defensive possession and finished the game with seven tackles.

Christian Benford, CB, toe

Christian Benford returned Monday after missing Buffalo's loss to New England in Week 4 because of a toe injury.

He left during the fourth quarter after tackling Puka Nacua and appeared to favor his right foot.

Benford returned later in the quarter and recorded 10 tackles in the win over the Rams.

Terrel Bernard, LB

Terrel Bernard left Monday night's game during the fourth quarter after going down while attempting to tackle Rams running back Kyren Williams.

Bernard missed one play before returning.

D.J. Moore, WR, shoulder

D.J. Moore was inactive against the Rams after aggravating his left shoulder injury during Buffalo's Week 4 loss to New England.

He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday.

Moore originally suffered the AC joint injury against the Detroit Lions in Week 2. He returned the following week against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Ed Oliver, DL, knee

Ed Oliver missed Monday night's game because of the knee injury he suffered against New England in Week 4.

Oliver did not practice at all last week.

The defensive tackle was injured during the third quarter against the Patriots when former Bills fullback Reggie Gilliam hit his left leg near the sideline.

Oliver also missed Buffalo's Week 2 victory over Detroit because of a hip injury.

Joshua Palmer, WR, shoulder

Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice.

Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday.

Bills coach Joe Brady said Saturday that Palmer got twisted up during practice.

Dee Alford, CB, ankle

Dee Alford missed Monday night's game because of the ankle injury he suffered in Week 4.

He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams.

Buffalo signed cornerback Anthony Kendall from the practice squad to the active roster before Monday's game, giving the secondary additional depth.

Landon Jackson, DL, knee

Landon Jackson did not play against the Rams.

He suffered a knee injury in Week 4 but returned to the game in the loss to the Patriots.

Buffalo Bills injured reserve

Zane Durant, DL, neck

Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve.

Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared.

Buffalo Bills physically unable to perform

Tyrell Shavers, WR, knee

Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list.

Shavers is recovering from the torn ACL he suffered during Buffalo's wild-card playoff victory last season.

The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready.

Buffalo Bills non-football injury

Dorian Strong, CB, neck

Las Vegas Raiders injury update for Week 6

Ashton Jeanty, RB, ankle/foot

Ashton Jeanty played against New England despite being listed as questionable because of ankle and foot injuries.

He rushed for 27 yards on 10 carries and caught five passes for 50 yards in the loss to the Patriots.

"Unless I can't run, jump, I'm playing. Football is a tough game. You're never gonna play feeling 100 percent," Jeanty said. "So at the end of the day, I just want to go out there and do my best for my teammates and whatever it takes."

Tonka Hemingway, DT, concussion

Tonka Hemingway left Sunday's loss to New England during the first quarter with what the Raiders initially announced as a neck injury.

He was ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Hemingway entered the NFL concussion protocol.

Jalen Nailor, WR, concussion

Jalen Nailor missed Sunday's loss to New England because of a concussion.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Nailor is expected to return to practice this week as he works through the NFL concussion protocol.

Patrick Johnson, DE, neck

Patrick Johnson left Sunday's loss to New England during the second quarter with a neck injury.

He did not return.

Trey Zuhn III, G, knee

Trey Zuhn III missed Sunday's game because of a knee injury.

title: NFL Must Face CTE Head-on - Marquette Wire
description:
But the problem is still the most pressing issue facing the NFL, and it’s not much closer to being resolved.
Based on NFL concussion data, the number of concussions per season has trended down over 30% from 2015 to 2025.
“But the big crisis facing the NFL and players — it’s CTE, not concussion.” According to Nowinski, 1 in 5 people diagnosed with CTE did not have a diagnosed concussion in their career.
A study published by the British Medical Journal revealed that at least 1 in 4 NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE.
Out of a sample of 338, 315 — or 93% — of the NFL players’ brains studied had the diagnosis of CTE.
text:
A “tormented soul.”

That was the title of a 2005 ESPN article about Mike Webster, the first NFL player diagnosed with progressive degenerative brain disease Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) after his death at age 50.

Webster was a broken man. He took a medley of narcotics to numb his pain from the headaches, depression and anxiety that beset him. He would repeatedly stun himself with a taser until he went unconscious — his son said it’s the only way he could fall asleep.

Almost 20 years later, public understanding of CTE has become more ubiquitous. But the problem is still the most pressing issue facing the NFL, and it’s not much closer to being resolved. The NFL needs to step up their game to confront the protracted CTE epidemic.

In 1994, the NFL Commissioner Paul Tagliabue directly dismissed the problem during a panel on the future of sports.

“I think [concussions] is one of these pack journalism issues, frankly,” Tagliabue said. “There is no increase in concussions, the number is relatively small… The problem is a journalist issue.”

It would take 15 years after Tagliabue’s words for the league to acknowledge the potential long-term effects of concussions.

Four years after Webster’s death, NFL Spokesman Greg Aiello told Alan Schwarz from The New York Times that “it’s quite obvious from the medical research that’s been done that concussions can lead to long-term problems.”

In an attempt to appear vigilant, the NFL has issued no shortage of rule changes aimed at reducing concussions. The most visible of all of them has been the guardian cap, a piece of protective padding that goes over the helmet.

The problem is that the guardian cap and the rules changes haven’t really moved the needle. Chris Nowinski, co-founder of the Concussion and CTE Foundation, called them a scam.

“It’s very clear from their behavior and the conversations I’ve had with them, they love that the public sees the Guardian Caps because it’s basically virtue signaling,” said Nowinski.

Based on NFL concussion data, the number of concussions per season has trended down over 30% from 2015 to 2025. But Nowinski is unmoved.

“You do want people to invest in tools that can reduce the risk of concussion. I do want NFL players to be safer,” Nowinski said. “But the big crisis facing the NFL and players — it’s CTE, not concussion.”

According to Nowinski, 1 in 5 people diagnosed with CTE did not have a diagnosed concussion in their career. CTE is a result of years of impacts, even if they are subconcussive.

Researchers are wrestling to understand the scale.

A study published by the British Medical Journal revealed that at least 1 in 4 NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE.

The authors say even that is a conservative estimate. Out of a sample of 338, 315 — or 93% — of the NFL players’ brains studied had the diagnosis of CTE.

Marc Weisskopf, a professor at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, pushes back on this study. He says the sampling bias distorts the real occurrence of the disease.

The study only analyzed 9% of the total NFL player population over that time period and since it only looked at autopsied brains, it wasn’t a random sample. This means it’s misleading to extrapolate the 1-in-4 statistic to the population as a whole.

The issue with studying CTE is that you can only diagnose postmortem. In order to make significant progress in understanding the extent of the problem and effective prevention strategies, a test on living players must be developed. The NFL should be much more invested in research to make this happen.

Various players from around the league have expressed interest in taking a test if it became available. The NFL generated $24 billion in revenue last year — they owe it to them. It’s the bare minimum for the severe risk of irreversibly altering players’ brains.

By most accounts, the Patriots' blowout win over the Raiders in Week 5 was a massive step forward for their offense. But TreVeyon Henderson's exit did bring some concern.

In the first half against Las Vegas, Henderson left the game with an ankle injury, later ruled out of the matchup.

As one of the more explosive weapons in the offense, Henderson has been a significant contributor since being drafted in the second round in 2025 — but based on the latest injury update, the Patriots will have to play without him for some time.

Here's the latest on Henderson and what it means for the Patriots' backfield.

TreVeyon Henderson Injury Update

Henderson was ruled out with an ankle injury during Sunday's 45-17 blowout win over the Raiders; he came up limping after being tackled by Jeremy Chinn on an 11-yard run.

Coach Mike Vrabel did not provide an update on him postgame, with Rhamondre Stevenson taking on a bigger workload than the usual split duties afterward. Corey Kiner also saw some action against Las Vegas.

Now, with the Patriots already dealing with injuries to A.J. Brown, Will Campbell and more, Henderson is set to miss some time. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Tuesday that Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain that is "expected to sideline him multiple weeks."

Henderson will not need surgery for the injury and is "regarded as a quick healer," but the Patriots will likely be playing multiple games without him.

New England is set for clashes with the Jets, Bears and Dolphins over the next three weeks — Henderson's injury doesn't come at a particularly tough period on the schedule, but the team will be hoping he can return soon.

By the time Henderson does come back, the Patriots may also have Brown back on the field to roll out the offense they envisioned this offseason.

Patriots RB Depth Chart

Stevenson and Henderson have remained one of the NFL's more split backfields, with both capable of catching passes for added versatility. Without Henderson, expect to see a heavier workload for the veteran, Stevenson, who has 227 rushing yards and two touchdowns so far in 2026.

However, second-year running back Corey Kiner will also take on a more significant role. He took six carries for 52 yards and one catch for seven yards in the big win over the Raiders, though he did fumble as well. Ball security will be critical for Kiner, but he looked like a potential contributor in Week 5.

Henderson's injury will likely mean a backfield focused on Stevenson, with Kiner mixing in more often as a change-of-pace option after impressing in Week 5.

LONDON -- Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will have arthroscopic surgery on his right knee when the team returns from London next week, league sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.

The team does not yet know the severity of the injury, which Harrison sustained during last Sunday's 19-17 victory over Philadelphia at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Depending on what surgeons find, Harrison could be out three to five weeks or the remainder of the regular season.

The Jaguars (4-1) play Houston (1-4) on Sunday at Wembley Stadium and are scheduled to fly back to Jacksonville after the game. Walker Little, who came in after Harrison's injury, is expected to start at left tackle.

Harrison was hurt while blocking on a running play, a sweep to the right by Bhayshul Tuten. Harrison appeared to grab his right knee after disengaging from a block and went down to the ground. He was eventually taken off the field on a cart.

Harrison, the 27th overall pick in 2023, was moved from right tackle to left tackle during training camp. He had missed just three games at right tackle in his first three seasons.

The Jaguars picked up Harrison's fifth-year option in April.

Sidelined since suffering a right hamstring injury against the Vikings on 20 September, the quarterback returned to practice in a limited capacity on Friday 9 October.

That progress was not enough to allow him to play in Green Bay, where Chicago fell 31-7.

The trip to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday 18 October now represents a possible return date.

But between resuming some drills and being able to run the Offense during a game, Williams still has the final stages of his recovery programme to work through.

What injury did Caleb Williams suffer?

Williams was hurt in the fourth quarter of the 9-3 defeat to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.

He had attempted to push forward down the left side on a play near the end zone before leaving the game.

Ben Johnson subsequently announced that his quarterback would be evaluated week to week, without setting a specific date for his return.

Since then, Williams has missed three consecutive games.

Why is his return to practice encouraging?

On Friday 9 October, Williams took part in a session in a limited capacity for the first time since his injury.

He was listed as questionable for the game against the Packers, even though Johnson had already announced that Tyson Bagent would start the game.

That designation applied solely to Week 5: it does not serve as an official indication of his availability against Atlanta.

In the report released by Chicago on Friday, Johnson explained that Williams was progressively increasing his running work and continuing a throwing programme.

The goal was to move forward step by step while ensuring that progression did not cause any setbacks.

The limited return therefore represents a genuine step forward, but not yet clearance to play.

What still needs to happen to confirm his return?

The question is no longer simply whether Williams can throw the ball.

The programme outlined by Johnson also includes a gradual increase in his movement and running work.

For a quarterback capable of extending plays and escaping the pocket, that dimension matters just as much as resuming his throwing.

Upcoming practice reports will allow his level of participation to be tracked.

A limited session means a player does not take part in all of the planned work; on its own, it is not enough to conclude he will be available on Sunday.

The Bears' decision will then need to be waited on, along with any potential designation on the final injury report.

Chicago has not publicly announced a specific number of sessions or a participation threshold that would guarantee his return.

Analysis: Chicago needs Williams, not a rushed return

Romain Champagne, DAZN NFL journalist

Caleb Williams returning would obviously give Ben Johnson's Offense far more options.

But the defeat in Green Bay should not turn his recovery into a race against the clock.

The Bears did not struggle solely at the quarterback position: their running game took a step back and their Defense conceded several explosive plays.

Williams will not automatically fix all of those problems.

In my view, Chicago's priority should above all be getting their starter back in conditions that allow him to genuinely use his abilities, rather than simply putting his name back on the game sheet.

With a record of 3-2, the Bears have maintained a competitive position during his absence.

The priority must be a sustainable return, not an immediate response to one bad day.
