title: Fantasy Football Week 6 Injury Report: CeeDee Lamb, David Montgomery, Deebo Samuel, More
authors: Bryan Toporek, Senior Contributor, Bryan Toporek, Senior Contributor
description:
Every week, we'll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup moving forward.
Running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London would still be must-starts even if Tagovailoa is under center, but tight end Kyle Pitts would be a fringe starter at best.
The Texans face the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6 and New York Giants in Week 7 before going on bye in Week 8.
They lost running back TreVeyon Henderson to an ankle injury and starting left tackle Will Campbell to a knee injury in the span of only three plays in the second quarter, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss.
Notable WR Injuries Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad) For the first four weeks of the season, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb almost single-handedly carried his fantasy managers.
text:
The first month of the 2026 NFL season was brutal on fantasy football managers from an injury perspective. A number of early-round draft picks missed at least one game in the first four weeks, including Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua, Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson and Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley.

Week 5 finally provided some reprieve to beleaguered managers.

That isn't to say that every fantasy football manager emerged unscathed, though. One consensus first-round pick did have an injury scare, although it sounds like he'll avoid missing significant time. A few other players suffered concussions that will put their Week 6 status into jeopardy.

Every week, we'll be breaking down the biggest injury news that could shape your fantasy football lineup moving forward. Let's dive into all of the most notable updates ahead of Week 6.

Notable QB Injuries

Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. (ribs)

Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. suffered an injury to his ribs at the end of regulation against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 5. He was able to return for one snap before the start of overtime, but backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa took over for him in the extra period (and immediately threw a game-ending interception).

Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday that the rib injury "is not considered serious," and Penix "might be able to return" for the Falcons' Week 6 game against the Chicago Bears. "But the team wants to be cautious and see him practice this week first before deciding on the next move," Schefter added.

Tagovailoa figures to draw the start if Penix can't go, but that would be a major downgrade for an offense that just started to find its footing. Running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London would still be must-starts even if Tagovailoa is under center, but tight end Kyle Pitts would be a fringe starter at best.

Notable RB Injuries

Texans RB David Montgomery (groin)

David Montgomery began his Houston Texans tenure with a bang by piling up 79 total yards and three touchdowns in his team's Week 1 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Over the next four weeks, he totaled 78 rushing yards, 48 receiving yards and zero touchdowns.

While the Texans finally got their first win of the season against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5, they lost Montgomery to a groin injury in the first half. On Monday, Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters that "we'll see how he continues to progress," but "right now, we're looking at a week-to-week injury there."

The Texans face the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6 and New York Giants in Week 7 before going on bye in Week 8. Woody Marks, who had 15 carries for 62 yards and four catches for 23 yards on Sunday, will be a must-start until Montgomery returns, even against the Jaguars' stout run defense.

Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle)

The New England Patriots blew out the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5, but it didn't come without a cost. They lost running back TreVeyon Henderson to an ankle injury and starting left tackle Will Campbell to a knee injury in the span of only three plays in the second quarter, according to ESPN's Mike Reiss.

Prior to his departure, Henderson had four carries for 22 yards and one reception for 16 yards. Rhamondre Stevenson led the way for the Pats on the ground with 13 carries for 64 yards and a touchdown along with three receptions for 21 yards, while Corey Kiner added six carries for 52 yards, most of which came during garbage time.

If Henderson isn't able to suit up against the New York Jets in Week 6, Stevenson would be a must-start (if he isn't already).

Browns RB Quinshon Judkins (ankle)

Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins didn't leave his team's Week 5 loss to the New York Jets early, but he was spotted in a walking boot after the game. On Monday, head coach Todd Monken said Judkins suffered a "tweak" in his ankle and is day-to-day, according to ESPN's Daniel Oyefusi.

The Browns also lost fellow running back Raheim Sanders to a hip injury on Sunday. That could help explain why they signed running back Audric Estime off the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad on Monday, as NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported.

Judkins finished Sunday's loss with 14 carries for 44 scoreless yards along with three receptions for six yards. Even if he's able to suit up in Week 6 against the Baltimore Ravens, it'll be difficult to start him with much confidence, particularly given the risk of reinjury.

Eagles RB Will Shipley (foot)

Will Shipley's time as the Philadelphia Eagles' starting running back was short-lived.

With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (core muscle) both sidelined, Shipley drew the start for the Eagles against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. However, he suffered "a partial tear of his plantar fascia," which "could sideline him multiple weeks," according to Schefter.

Bigsby is on injured reserve, so he's guaranteed to miss at least three more weeks, although Barkley appears to be nearing his return. If none of Barkley, Bigsby and Shipley can go in Week 6, the Eagles would be down to practice-squad call-ups such as Dameon Pierce or off-the-street free agents, none of whom would be worth starting in 10- or 12-team leagues.

Notable WR Injuries

Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad)

For the first four weeks of the season, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb almost single-handedly carried his fantasy managers. In Week 5, however, he finished with a season-low two catches for nine yards before departing the Cowboys' loss late with a quadriceps injury.

On Friday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Lamb suffered a quad bruise that is "not believed to be serious." He added that the Cowboys "do not expect this to be a long-term injury," although he did not say that Lamb is certain to play in Week 6.

Ryan Flournoy could be worth a spot start if Lamb does miss the Cowboys' game against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday Night Football, although the passing offense would likely be funneled through George Pickens. Pickens is a must-start either way, but he'd have top-five WR upside without Lamb hogging targets.

49ers WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring)

The San Francisco 49ers have been churning through wide receivers faster than Spinal Tap went through drummers. After losing Ricky Pearsall (knee), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle), Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Christian Kirk (calf) earlier this season, the Niners took another hit in Week 5 when Deebo Samuel suffered a hamstring injury in the third quarter of their win over the Seattle Seahawks.

After the game, Samuel was "moving slowly in the team's locker room," according to ESPN's Nick Wagoner, although head coach Kyle Shanahan said he didn't know the severity of Samuel's injury. However, Shanahan told reporters Monday that Samuel will miss "at least a couple of weeks" because of his hamstring injury.

The Niners play the Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football in Week 6 and face the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 before their Week 8 bye. There's almost zero chance Samuel returns until Week 9 at the earliest, which means the Niners' passing offense is more or less down to WR Mike Evans, TE George Kittle and RB Christian McCaffrey for now.

Steelers WRs Michael Pittman Jr. (foot), Roman Wilson (finger)

The Pittsburgh Steelers lost a trio of wide receivers within the past week.

Michael Pittman Jr. aggravated a foot injury in practice Wednesday that landed him on injured reserve, which seemingly opened the door for third-year wideout Roman Wilson to carve out a bigger role in the short term.

Across Weeks 3 and 4, Wilson caught six passes for 134 yards and two touchdowns. In Week 5, though, he had zero catches on one target before leaving the game with a finger injury that's expected to sideline him for multiple weeks, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy already announced that Wilson won't play in Week 6.

That wasn't the only bad news McCarthy delivered on Monday. He also announced wideout Ben Skowronek, who left Sunday's game with a calf injury, won't play in Week 6.

Steelers rookie wideout Germie Bernard, who caught a career-high six passes for 80 yards against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5, might be one of the top waiver-wire pickups of the week given the injuries besieging Pittsburgh's receiving corps. Tight end Pat Freiermuth and running back Jaylen Warren should stay busy in the passing game moving forward, too.

Browns WR KC Concepcion (concussion)

Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion found himself on the wrong end of a scary-looking helmet-to-helmet hit by New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick with five minutes left in the first quarter on Sunday. He stayed on the ground "for multiple minutes before being helped to his feet by Cleveland's medical staff," according to Oyefusi, and he was quickly ruled out with a concussion.

Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase suffered a concussion in Week 4 and was able to clear the NFL's concussion protocol in time to play in Week 5, but every concussion is different. There's no guarantee that Concepcion will clear the protocol in time to play against the division-rival Baltimore Ravens in Week 6.

Isaiah Bond, Denzel Boston and Jerry Jeudy each had three catches on seven targets in Concepcion's absence on Sunday, although Bond led the way with 74 receiving yards, while Boston scored the Browns' lone touchdown. Boston would be the only Browns receiver worth starting if Concepcion isn't back against the Ravens.

Notable TE Injuries

Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson (concussion)

Unfortunately, Concepcion wasn't the only fantasy-relevant player to suffer a concussion in Week 5. Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson also did after catching a seven-yard pass on the second play of the game in his team's win over the New Orleans Saints.

As Hockenson was being tackled, his head drove straight into the Superdome turf. "He remained on the ground for several minutes before jogging to the sideline and later the locker room for a concussion test," according to ESPN's Kevin Seifert.

The Vikings are on bye in Week 6, so Hockenson will have an extra week to clear the NFL's concussion protocol before potentially missing a game. The Vikings lost backup tight end Josh Oliver to a torn biceps muscle in Week 4, which left them with only Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek at tight end after Hockenson departed. Neither would be worth starting if Hockenson doesn't clear the concussion protocol by Week 7.

Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq (concussion)

In Week 3, New York Jets rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq exploded with a career-high seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown. The following week, he finished with zero catches for zero yards on four targets, and in Week 5, he had two catches for three yards on three targets before departing in the third quarter with a concussion.

After the game, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that Sadiq "checked out just fine," but he still needs to go through the NFL's concussion protocol. Just like with Hockenson and Concepcion, there's no guarantee that Sadiq will clear the protocol in time to suit up for Week 6.

Even if Sadiq does play, he's gone from a fringe TE1 to a touchdown-dependent TE2. You shouldn't be starting him unless you're in a 16-team league or are desperate for a healthy body at that position.

Returning Soon?

Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle)

Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed his team's Week 5 overtime win against the Falcons with an "unconventional" ankle sprain. However, Rapoport reported Monday that the Ravens have "some hope" Jackson will be back for their Week 6 game against the division-rival Browns.

The Ravens went extremely run-heavy against the Falcons with Tyler Huntley under center in place of Jackson. It wouldn't be a surprise if they went that route against Cleveland as well, which means fantasy managers would have to keep their expectations in check for wide receiver Zay Flowers in particular.

Eagles RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring), WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring)

The Eagles have been without running back Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wide receiver DeVonta Smith for the past two weeks because of hamstring injuries. But on Monday, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni suggested help may be on the way this week.

According to Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, "indications are one, if not both" of Smith and Barkley "have a shot to return" against the Carolina Panthers in Week 6. However, Garafolo noted the Eagles "have to see how the practice week goes" before making that determination.

If either (or both) do return, they'll be lining up with an almost entirely new offensive line in the wake of Lane Johnson's retirement and the trade of Cam Jurgens. But with both Bigsby and Shipley expected to be unavailable for Week 6, the Eagles badly need Barkley back ASAP in particular.

Patriots WR A.J. Brown (ankle)

New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in the season opener that was originally expected to sideline him for 6-8 weeks. He might beat that timetable, as Garafolo reported last week that New England's "hope is" that Brown is back in the fold by Week 6.

On Monday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters that "there's a chance" Brown will begin practice this week. With quarterback Drake Maye having regained his mojo after an early-season slump, Brown will immediately deserve a spot back in fantasy lineups whenever he's able to return.

title: UCLA QB Nico Iamaleava expected to miss remainder of season after knee injury
description:
UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.
A former five-star recruit, Iamaleava transferred from Tennessee to UCLA prior to the 2025 season, and he stuck with the Bruins after Chesney took charge.
In his second season with the Bruins, Iamaleava provided some stability at the quarterback position, even if his numbers didn't jump off the page.
Dieffenbach's resume -- or lack thereof -- probably leaves the door open for sophomore Madden Iamaleava, Nico's younger brother.
Madden Iamaleava has even less experience, limited to one passing attempt in his career.
text:
UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. Iamaleava exited Saturday's 17-15 win over Oregon after getting tangled up awkwardly between a pair of Ducks defenders.

At his Monday press conference, Bob Chesney admitted there was "serious concern' but didn't officially rule out Iamaleava for the rest of the season.

"I'm gonna wait on our doctors to make the final call on things," Chesney said. "He has a meeting later today, and we'll have a lot more clarity on where things are at. ... There is serious concern at the moment, but at the same time, there's nothing that has been fully ruled at this time. There's still other opinions and people we want to talk to just to make sure everyone sees it the same way."

A former five-star recruit, Iamaleava transferred from Tennessee to UCLA prior to the 2025 season, and he stuck with the Bruins after Chesney took charge. In his second season with the Bruins, Iamaleava provided some stability at the quarterback position, even if his numbers didn't jump off the page.

In four-plus games, Iamaleava completed 62.1 percent of his passes for 982 yards, four touchdowns and four interceptions while rushing for 144 yards and a score.

Looking ahead to the offseason, Iamaleava will have a big decision to make regarding the 2027 NFL Draft. Iamaleava has the tools to be an early-round selection, but he may have to spend one more season at the college level to prove his health and boost his draft stock.

When Iamaleava left the game against Oregon, backup Ty Dieffenbach entered and managed the offense well enough to get the win. The senior completed three of his six passing attempts for 43 yards and a touchdown.

No. 12 UCLA's first test without Iamaleava will be a home contest against 4-1 Wisconsin on Saturday night.

Where do the Bruins go at QB?

While Dieffenbach replaced Iamaleava against Oregon, that doesn't mean the starting role is his for the rest of the season. In his postgame press conference, Chesney admitted it will be a "week-to-week" situation and that Dieffenbach's mobility earned him the nod as the primary back against Oregon.

"We're really on a week-to-week basis here," Chesney told 247Sports. "This week, we felt like we had to run a little bit more with the quarterback, possibly. And that's where I thought Ty had a really nice week. And that put us in that spot. It's just one of those things. I'm sure if Madden had gone in there, he would have done a phenomenal job as well. But Ty was the guy we decided on based on the previous week of practice, and I thought he did a really good job. But Madden is going to be there the whole way through as well, competing and fighting for that position with or without Nico."

Although he performed admirably, Dieffenbach's appearance against Oregon was his FBS debut. A three-star recruit out of high school, Dieffenbach spent two years at Pitt before transferring to Cal Poly last season. He was the Mustangs' starter last year before transferring to UCLA in the offseason.

In his lone season at Cal Poly, Dieffenbach completed just 56.8 percent of his passes for 1,305 yards, nine touchdowns and nine interceptions.

Dieffenbach's resume -- or lack thereof -- probably leaves the door open for sophomore Madden Iamaleava, Nico's younger brother. A four-star recruit in the 2025 signing class, Madden spent a few months at Arkansas before joining his brother at UCLA.

Madden Iamaleava has even less experience, limited to one passing attempt in his career. It fell incomplete.

This may be a scenario in which Chesney simply rides the hot hand from one week to another, but the good news is that the quarterback probably won't be asked to do much.

How much does QB matter?

The quarterback definitely matters, since the Bruins can't play someone who derails the entire offense. But can Chesney find a game manager between Dieffenbach and Madden Iamaleava? That may be all he needs.

If Chesney can get average quarterback play the rest of the way, then UCLA's College Football Playoff hopes are very much still alive because of how good the team is at running the ball and playing defense.

The Bruins rank sixth in the country in rushing yards per game with 253.2, and Wayne Knight is budding into a national superstar at running back. That should allow UCLA to take some of the burden off its quarterback, whoever that may be.

It also helps that the Bruins don't need to light up the scoreboard because of how the defense is playing. The Bruins are eighth in the Big Ten in scoring defense, allowing just 18.0 points per game, and they're especially good against the run, surrendering just 87.6 rushing yards per game.

That means the quarterback doesn't have to air the ball out to win. In fact, Nico Iamaleava wasn't exactly turning heads with his play before the injury. The elder Iamaleava brother turned the ball over three times against Oregon, and UCLA still managed to pull out a win in Autzen Stadium.

description:

Jackson sprained his ankle in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans, and the injury sidelined him in practice last week and in Sunday’s comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons.
Minter said Jackson is “definitely doing better,” but he acknowledged that it’s too early to know whether Jackson would be available to practice Wednesday.

The third-round pick broke his wrist in the Ravens’ season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts.

Join the huddle. Sign up here for Ravens updates in your inbox.

Quarterback Lamar Jackson is “doing everything he can” to return in time for the Ravens’ game Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, but coach Jesse Minter said Monday that his recovery timetable is unclear.

Jackson sprained his ankle in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans, and the injury sidelined him in practice last week and in Sunday’s comeback win over the Atlanta Falcons. Tyler Huntley started in his place, going 24-for-32 for 201 yards and two touchdowns and adding a score on a quarterback sneak.

Minter said Jackson is “definitely doing better,” but he acknowledged that it’s too early to know whether Jackson would be available to practice Wednesday.

“Again, he’s doing everything he can,” said Minter, who noted last week that Jackson wouldn’t need to practice to be cleared to play. “I think we’ll know more, definitely, by the middle of the week.”

The Ravens are 3-0 over the past two seasons in games that Huntley has started. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman called him an “overly prepared backup.”

“It’s hard to back up a guy like Lamar Jackson and to come in [with] certain situations like he has in his career,” Bateman said Sunday. “It is big. It shows that he’s always ready for the moment, for the game and for the right play call to be called.”

Jurgens in ‘finishing stages’

Rookie Vega Ioane’s two-game stint at center might end on a high note, with Cam Jurgens approaching the end of the NFL’s concussion protocol.

Ioane, who was thrust into the starting job after injuries to Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic, is expected to return to right guard once Jurgens is available. The Ravens traded for the two-time Pro Bowl pick last week.

After missing practice last week with symptoms stemming from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 4 game, Jurgens is now in the “finishing stages” of the protocol, Minter said, and “signs point in a good direction for Cam to be ready to play.”

Jurgens has spent his downtime studying coordinator Declan Doyle’s offense, and Minter said the team feels good about where he stands mentally and physically.

Others nearing return

Rookie wide receiver and training camp sensation Ja’Kobi Lane, who’s eligible to come off injured reserve this week, could return to practice Wednesday.

The third-round pick broke his wrist in the Ravens’ season-opening win over the Indianapolis Colts. Minter said his conditioning is in “a really good place.”

Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, the Ravens’ top pass rusher and biggest free-agent signing, is also “chomping at the bit” to return to the field after undergoing surgery on his finger. He’s missed the past two games.

“We’ll see how that shakes out on Wednesday, but I feel pretty good about both those guys,” Minter said.

The Ravens left Atlanta without any major injuries, Minter said. They had a few players briefly leave the game, including right tackle Roger Rosengarten, defensive linemen Travis Jones and Broderick Washington, and tight end Matt Hibner, but they all returned to the field.

Green Bay Packers defensive tackle Javon Hargrave will miss the rest of the season with a torn Achilles.

The injury occurred late in the fourth quarter of the Packers' victory over the Chicago Bears.

Hargrave signed a two-year, $23-million deal with the Packers in March.

GREEN BAY – The debut season is over for Green Bay Packers defensive tackle Javon Hargrave.

Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles to end his season.

Hargrave went down and was carted off the field late in the fourth quarter of the Packers' 31-7 victory over the rival Chicago Bears.

"It was unfortunate. I know it took a lot of wind out of my sails last night after the game," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Oct. 12 about Hargrave's injury. "When you have a devastating injury like that to anybody, let alone a guy that's come in here, and done things the right way, and been a real asset to our football team."

The 33-year-old signed a two-year, $23-million deal with the Packers in March after spending the 2025 season with the Minnesota Vikings. Hargrave had 52 tackles, 3.5 sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in 16 games for the Vikings last season.

Hargrave played in four of the Packers' first five games, missing the Week 2 game against the New York Jets with a knee injury and concussion.

He recorded six total tackles (two solo) and one pass defended for the Packers.

The Packers defense now has suffered two Achilles injuries in as many games, coming a week after star linebacker Edgerrin Cooper went down against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Once one of the deepest positions on the team, the defensive tackle room has dealt with injuries. In addition to Hargrave, Warren Brinson was placed on injured reserve on Oct. 3 due to a groin injury, Anthony Campbell has missed the last three games to an ankle injury, and the Packers are still waiting for Jordon Riley to return from his Achilles injury he suffered at the end of the 2025 season.

LaFleur said he felt Riley is "pretty close" and hopes Campbell will be back this week.

"It truly is a next-man-up mentality," LaFleur said. "Guys got to get ready to play. That's just the nature of the beast."

text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers will be without yet another of their top receivers for the foreseeable future after Deebo Samuel Sr. suffered a hamstring injury in Sunday's win against the Seattle Seahawks.

After further testing on Samuel's right hamstring Monday, Niners coach Kyle Shanahan said that the injury "got him pretty good" and that the receiver is "going to miss some time." It's unclear exactly how much time Samuel will miss, but the Niners know they will be without him for at least the next couple of games and likely a bit longer.

The same is true of backup linebacker Garret Wallow, who also suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. Shanahan, while noting that the injury is "not quite as bad" as Samuel's, said Wallow will miss "at least a couple of weeks."

Samuel left Sunday's 32-29 win against Seattle with 5:06 left in the third quarter. Although he'd been favoring the right leg earlier, Samuel didn't exit for good until he was tackled by Seahawks linebacker Drake Thomas on the left sideline.

As Samuel went to the ground, he landed on the ball and then lost it. As he attempted to recover it, Samuel couldn't reel it back in and then stayed down.

The Niners medical staff ran out to help Samuel, who took a few minutes to get up and slowly make his way back to the sideline. The 49ers ruled out Samuel's potential return almost immediately.

The 49ers are down four of the top five wideouts they hoped to have entering the season. Ricky Pearsall (knee), De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) are on injured reserve.

Robinson is the closest to returning, though he's not eligible to open his 21-day practice window until after next Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders. He has been doing conditioning on a side field during practice in the past week.

Veteran Christian Kirk (calf) is on IR as well and eligible to return to practice, though Shanahan indicated that isn't likely to happen this week.

The 49ers enter Week 6 with Mike Evans, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing as the available receivers on the roster. The team also has Will Pauling, Xavier Smith and Malik Turner on the practice squad.

"I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look."

Wallow's injury in tandem with the one-game suspension for starting weakside linebacker Dre Greenlaw complicates matters for the Niners at linebacker at least for next week's game.

The Niners will lean on rookie Jaden Dugger with Luke Gifford and Tatum Bethune offering depth, but they could need to dip into the practice squad for Jalen Graham if Greenlaw's appeal is unsuccessful.

Shanahan said linebacker Nick Martin, who is on IR with a hamstring injury, is getting close and the team might look into opening his practice window this week.

In better injury news for the 49ers, Shanahan said defensive end Nick Bosa (calf), fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. (ankle) could return this week.

"[They're] all kind of in the same boat," Shanahan said. "They all got a chance, but definitely not saying they're good to go right now. We've got to continue to evaluate them throughout the week and it'll take all week, but hopefully they can get there."

text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers look like they're about to lose another one of their top wide receivers for a sustained period of time.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Roman Wilson is expected to be out for a few weeks after suffering a finger injury at the end of the first half of the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

"Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a couple of weeks due to a finger injury suffered Sunday, per source," Fowler wrote on X. "He’s still gathering info and seeking a second opinion."

Steelers Have Real WR Concerns Now

Pittsburgh is dealing with significant injury concerns across the board at wide receiver.

Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on the reserve/injured list on October 10 after aggravating his foot injury last week. The 29-year-old, who originally missed the team's Week 2 game against the New England Patriots, is dealing with plantar fasciitis and won't be back on the field until Week 10 at the absolute earliest.

Alongside Wilson, Ben Skowronek sustained a calf injury in the first half against Indianapolis and missed the rest of the contest from that point forward.

DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen are the only healthy receivers remaining on the 53-man roster. Brandon Smith was also active against the Colts, though he was a practice squad elevation.

Where Does Pittsburgh Go from Here?

The obvious short-term solution for the Steelers is to sign Smith to the 53-man roster.

The 27-year-old training camp standout played 16 snaps on offense vs. Indianapolis and has two practice squad elevations left, but there's now an opening for him on the 53-man roster.

Wetjen is strictly a kick returner and has yet to see the field on offense as a rookie, though, so Pittsburgh will have to make another move or two at receiver now that Wilson seems set to miss multiple games.

Bernard proved that he can start next to Metcalf by posting 80 yards on six catches against the Colts, and the Steelers have the luxury of being able to run a ton of 12 personnel with Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington at tight end, but they still need another real option at receiver.

Whether it's making an early trade nearly a month before the November 10 trade deadline or bringing in a veteran free agent, Pittsburgh has to get aggressive and be extremely diligent in filling its hole at receiver in the coming days.

text:
During the first quarter of the Cleveland Browns' Week 5 matchup against the New York Jets, rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion was knocked out of the game with a head injury.

Jets defensive back Minkah Fitzpatrick was flagged for a facemask after ripping Concepcion's helmet off following a catch from quarterback Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's second offensive drive. Later in the same drive, Concepcion was leveled and lay motionless on the field at MetLife Stadium.

He was quickly ruled out with a head injury. On Monday, the CFR confirmed that Concepcion has entered the NFL's concussion protocol.

1/1Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE

After the game, Browns head coach Todd Monken dismissed the notion that Fitzpatrick's hit on the rookie wideout was dirty, calling it a "bang-bang play."

On the CFR YouTube channel Monday afternoon, former Browns offensive tackle Chris Hubbard disagreed with that assessment.

"It was very scary, honestly," Hubbard said. "I don't think it was a bang-bang play to me, it was one of those scary sights and nothing could've been done."

Fitzpatrick was flagged for a hit on a defenseless receiver and could face a fine from the NFL. The play is also likely to renew scrutiny of his history of questionable hits. In 2023, while a member of the Pittsburgh Steelers, Fitzpatrick injured Nick Chubb on a hit that the Browns running back later said changed the course of his career.

‌

"I've played against (Fitzpatrick) multiple times and I've seen him take shots that are late and very questionable," Hubbard said. "Like what are your intentions when you're out there and a player is like that?"

Hubbard explained that the NFL is a brotherhood and a community. While players compete fiercely against one another, there is an understanding that they have a responsibility to protect each other from unnecessary injury.

On Monday morning, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn also defended Fitzpatrick.

"Minkah is not a dirty player," Glenn said. "He's never been a dirty player."

Concepcion's injury cost him the final three quarters of Sunday's game against the Jets. After entering the NFL's concussion protocol Monday, the rookie could also miss Cleveland's Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Regardless of whether Fitzpatrick is fined, the immediate concern for Cleveland is Concepcion's health and the potential loss of a key piece of its offense.

‌

With Concepcion sidelined, the Browns turned to Isaiah Bond. The results were far from encouraging.

Before Week 5, CFR VIP members learned that Cleveland was not the mystery team pursuing former Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. The report also detailed the Browns' desire to get Concepcion and Denzel Boston more involved in their weekly game plans. Eventually, Cleveland could even consider trading veteran receiver Jerry Jeudy to open up opportunities for Bond.

But the 22-year-old caught just three of his seven targets against the Jets, dropping crucial passes that made an already difficult day worse for Watson. Bond still has considerable development ahead of him before he can consistently contribute to winning efforts in the NFL.

Had Concepcion remained healthy, Bond likely would have seen fewer opportunities Sunday. Instead, his struggles became another problem for a Browns offense that couldn't do enough to beat the Jets.

The Browns can't change what happened to Concepcion. But with a crucial AFC North matchup against Baltimore looming, they may have to find another way to replace his production if the rookie is unable to play.

The Cleveland Browns are 3-2 after losing to the New York Jets in Week 5.

But the most concerning part wasn't the 17-12 final score.

It's the fact that the Browns weren't able to overcome the same mistakes they've been making throughout all five games this season. In their three straight comeback wins, the Browns masked some of the real landmines that exist within this team.

The Browns "only" had six penalties on Sunday against the Jets. For their standards, that's not bad. But they mostly came in soul-crushing moments, for undisciplined acts, in the a pivotal swing game.

4-1 certainly would've felt better than 3-2, especially with the Baltimore Ravens on the horizon. The Browns have much more than penalties to clean up before they can start thinking about Week 6. After losing to that Jets team, any conversation about the NFL Playoffs might need to go on hold, and conversations about the NFL Draft could be closer than we realize.

The overall offensive game plan

It was never feasible for the Browns to play like relative crap for three quarters and then pull a rabbit out of a hat for 16 straight games.

On a rainy day in New Jersey, the Browns struggled to run the football, and it exposed a lot of the flaws with this offense. Quarterback Deshaun Watson might've looked like the best runner on the field, which isn't good, especially considering the fact that starting running back Quinshon Judkins was spotted in a walking boot after the game.

Judkins hasn't been impactful. The offensive line has been bad. But he doesn't have much vision at all. The CFR's Dylan Feltovich implored the Browns to add a running back before the trade deadline during the postgame show on YouTube. The conversation needs to be had about the 22-year-old running back who might've just injured the same leg as last season.

Heading into the fourth quarter, Denzel Boston and Harold Fannin Jr. combined had four targets. In a game where KC Concepcion was ruled out in the first quarter, that's just unacceptable.

Watson and head coach Todd Monken will likely hide behind verbal shields of "we don't control where the ball goes!" or "it's just about the open receiver!" but they need to find a way to get the ball into the hands of Boston and Fannin much earlier in games.

It's that simple.

Monken blamed Watson's eight sacks on the lack of a run game.

Unless the Browns can find a way to run the football, these offensive issues will likely persist. The head coach of the team is right about that. Watson wasn't Cleveland's biggest problem on Sunday, but it certainly looked like the Jets had figured out blitzing him.

Defenses are going to learn that at this stage in his career, Watson is a limited quarterback with a bit of athletic upside. Monken had schemed things up nicely for him in the first three weeks of the season, but after losing Concepcion, the offensive rhythm was lost in Week 5.

The Jets loaded the box, and it made life really difficult on the Browns without a run game.

On Sunday morning, conversations about the NFL Playoffs didn't feel too crazy, especially if they could've beaten the Jets. ESPN noted that 3-1 teams have a mathematical 75% chance of making the postseason in the current format. But the Browns have plenty of demons that need to be exercised before playoffs are a serious conversation for this season.

And unfortunately, Monken confessed he doesn't have an immediate solution to fixing the run game. A few weeks ago, he wasn't sure how to clean up the penalties, and they haven't stopped.

If these issues persist, the Browns have just as good of a chance to be selecting near the top of the 2027 NFL Draft.

text:
Michael Penix Jr. couldn’t finish the Sunday Night Football loss to the Baltimore Ravens after getting drilled in the ribs late; he actually returned briefly after Tua Tagoviloa took the field for a single play but was in too much pain to return for overtime. The worry was that Penix, who despite some very real hiccups against Baltimore has given this passing game a massive boost over the past three weeks, might miss a game or multiple games owing to his injury.

The team hasn’t confirmed this yet, but Adam Schefter reports that it’s a relatively minor rib injury—as minor as those get, given that they’re not particularly fun to go through—and Penix may actually be able to start in Week 6. The days ahead will tell the tale.

This is a relief for multiple reasons. The first is that you could tell when he took the hit that Penix was hurt, and the fact that Tagovailoa had to finish the game meant we were bracing for Atlanta’s starter to be out a while. Ideally he would not miss the Chicago game given that the Bears have a very gettable pass defense, but even if he does, the fact that this doesn’t seem likely to stretch out multiple weeks is a major relief. The second is that not having Penix on the field opens the door to a horror show of backup quarterback options headlined by Tua, who has as many interceptions in three passes (1) as Penix has in three weeks and 77 attempts. Perhaps Tagovailoa will look a lot better not having to come into the game cold, but I’m not particularly eager to find out.

Kevin Stefanski said he’ll likely have an update on Wednesday, but it sounds like the Falcons and Penix may have dodged a more serious, long-term outcome here. We’ll learn more as the week rolls on.

These are some of the most important injuries to watch after Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season.

text:
NFL Week 5 injury roundup: Deebo Samuel, TreVeyon Henderson and more appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The injuries are beginning to pile up now that the NFL calendar has flipped to October. Now that five weeks have come and gone, the main narratives of the season are beginning to come into focus. Injuries play an important role in that process, as an injury to a quarterback or other key player can torpedo a team's chances of competing.

These are some of the most important injuries to watch after Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season.

TreVeyon Henderson, New England Patriots

The Patriots got a huge win on Sunday and put together their second straight dominant performance. Their slow start to the season now looks more fluky than anything.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Unfortunately, New England lost their explosive second-year running back to an ankle injury in Week 5. Henderson was unable to play in Week 1 because of an injury and now could miss more time. Henderson had been splitting carries with Rhamondre Stevenson, so losing him for an extended stretch could be a problem for the Patriots.

In other Patriots injury news, left tackle Will Campbell was ruled out with a knee injury on Sunday. Campbell was reportedly in good spirits after beating the Raiders, which is a positive sign.

Campbell will have an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of his injury.

Deebo Samuel, San Francisco 49ers

Samuel suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks on Sunday. The team is awaiting MRI results to determine the severity of the injury. But early reports indicate that Samuel could miss some time.

NFL insider Ian Rapoport read the context clues and came away concerned about how quickly San Francisco ruled him out.

"Judging from the context clues, as we call it… the fact that the 49ers ruled Deebo Samuel out immediately is not a good sign," Rapoport said on SNY on Monday morning.

The 49ers have already lost De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, Christian Kirk, and Demarcus Robinson to injured reserve this season. Losing Deebo may not be a fatal blow to their offense, but it would put the 5-0 team in a vulnerable position pretty early in the year.

Michael Penix Jr., Atlanta Falcons

The Falcons will only go as far as Penix will take them during the 2026 season.

Atlanta was 0-2 without Penix and immediately went on a two-game winning streak after getting him back. But their fortunes changed once again on Sunday after Penix suffered a rib injury on Sunday Night Football.

Penix will have an MRI on his ribs on Monday to determine if he will miss any time. Those test results will play a huge part in determining where Atlanta goes from here. But at this point, it is at least good to see that Penix is already confident about returning next week.

Falcons fans should stay tuned for updates about Penix on Monday and throughout the week. If he is unable to play in Week 6, Atlanta's offense will not look the same.

Javon Hargrave, Green Bay Packers

The Packers got an absolutely huge win against the Bears on Sunday. Green Bay was in danger of losing all hope if they couldn't come up with the win. But now another defensive injury should have fans concerned despite the huge divisional win.

Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave left Sunday's game with what looked like a serious leg injury. Head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed to reporters that Hargrave is believed to have torn his Achilles. If confirmed, that would end his 2026 season. It would also make him the second Packers defender to suffer a season-ending injury over the past two weeks.

The Packers cannot afford to lose any more defensive talent before getting Micah Parsons back from his torn ACL.

Packers receiver Skyy Moore was also ruled out of Sunday's game after suffering an ankle injury.

David Montgomery, Houston Texans

Montgomery's production has absolutely fallen off a cliff after a strong Week 1 performance. His latest injury will not help matters at all.

The 29-year-old running back suffered a groin injury against the Titans. He left the game and was quickly ruled as out for the rest of the contest. Montgomery only managed five carries for 11 rushing yards before the injury. It would not be surprising to see Woody Marks take over as the team's top running back, or at least get his opportunity to win the job.

In other Texans injury news, Jalen Pitre suffered a shoulder injury against the Titans. He did not return.

Jalyx Hunt, Philadelphia Eagles

The Eagles couldn't even make good plays in London without something bad happening to them. That's exactly what happened on the final play of the first half.

Hunt attempted to pick up a fumble after Philly made a crucial stop on fourth-and-goal. Unfortunately, Hunt landed awkwardly on his leg and appeared to suffer a lower-leg injury. He refused the cart, but was helped off the field during halftime and did not return to the game.

Philadelphia was already without Jonathan Greenard on the edge. If Hunt ends up missing time, it will put even more pressure on the Eagles' depth to pick up the slack.

In other Eagles injury news, Will Shipley was ruled out after suffering a foot injury in London. That puts Philadelphia in a tough spot with only Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele healthy at the running back position.

T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings

The Vikings improved to 5-0 on the season, but it came at the cost of one offensive player.

Hockenson suffered a concussion during Sunday's contest. He left the field and did not return after being diagnosed with a concussion. If Hockenson wants to play in Week 6, he'll need to breeze through concussion protocol as quickly as possible. That is not a ridiculous goal, as Ja'Marr Chase just pulled off the same feat after last week's injury.

Now is a terrible time for Hockenson to suffer such an injury. He exploded in Week 4, hauling in all 13 of his targets for 119 receiving yards.

Other notable injuries from Week 5 include Browns receiver KC Concepcion (head injury), Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring), Ravens defensive tackle Broderick Washington (ankle), Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and Jets tight end Kenyon Sadiq (concussion).

text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have another injury concern on their defensive line following Sunday's blowout loss to the New England Patriots.

Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway has entered the NFL's concussion protocol after leaving the Raiders' 45-17 defeat in the first quarter.

The development puts his availability for Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills in question.

Hemingway initially left the Patriots game with what was described as a stinger or neck injury. He went to the locker room for further evaluation and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the contest.

On Monday, Hemingway was confirmed to be in concussion protocol ahead of the Week 6 matchup with Buffalo.

That doesn't automatically rule him out against the Bills, but he must complete the NFL's concussion protocol before he can return to game action.

The injury comes at a difficult time for a Raiders defense looking to rebound from its worst performance of the season.

New England piled up 536 yards of total offense Sunday, including 165 on the ground, as Las Vegas suffered its second consecutive loss after opening the season with three straight victories.

The Raiders' defensive struggles against New England were particularly troubling after the unit had shown promise during the team's 3-0 start.

The former South Carolina standout has become a contributor in the middle of the Raiders' defensive front during his second NFL season.

Through five games, Hemingway has recorded 14 combined tackles, according to the team's official statistics, including one in his abbreviated appearance against New England.

He has provided interior depth alongside Adam Butler, Thomas Booker, Jonah Laulu and Fatukasi.

If Hemingway cannot play against Buffalo, the Raiders could need additional snaps from their other defensive linemen as they prepare to face another challenging opponent.

Las Vegas has already struggled to contain opposing rushing attacks, a problem that continued against New England.

The Patriots added to those difficulties Sunday, consistently finding room to run while controlling the line of scrimmage.

The performance raised broader questions about whether the Raiders can regroup after their lopsided loss.

Hemingway's health, however, presents a more immediate concern.

The NFL's concussion protocol requires players to complete a five-step process and receive clearance from both the team physician and an independent neurological consultant before returning to game action.

There is no fixed timetable for completing the process, leaving Hemingway's status for Sunday uncertain.

The Raiders' upcoming practice reports should provide a clearer indication of his progress ahead of the Buffalo game.

For now, Las Vegas faces the possibility of entering Week 6 without one of its young defensive-line contributors.

The Atlanta Falcons lost starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. to a rib injury late in Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens. The third-year QB took a big hit while attempting to lead the Falcons to a game-winning field goal in the final seconds.

Head coach Kevin Stefanski said he would need to see imaging before giving an update on Penix, but that's why we have NFL insiders. According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Falcons are optimistic that Penix will play against the Chicago Bears in Week 6.

"There is optimism in Atlanta that QB Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) will be able to play Sunday against the Bears, sources tell The Athletic." Jones reported. "Penix missed overtime last night as the injury worsened as he sat."

ESPN's Adam Schefter had a similar report and said the team wants to see Penix in practice before determining whether or not he'll play in Week 6.

"Michael Penix’s rib injury is not considered serious, per sources," wrote Schefter. "Penix might be able to return for Sunday’s game vs. the Bears, but the team wants to be cautious and see him practice this week before it knows whether he will be able to play in Week 6."

As for Stefanski, he did not provide an update on Penix's health during his Monday press conference but said he expected to know more about the injury on Wednesday.

The Falcons will face the Bears on Sunday at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Chicago is still waiting to get quarterback Caleb Williams back, but there's reportedly a chance he could return in Week 6. The injury report will tell us a lot this week.

text:
Zac Taylor and the Bengals are back from Florida, with no major injuries added to the ledger after a rough week on that front. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins got through the game without any setbacks, and Zac Taylor discussed the team's overall health before entering the official bye week window.

Cincinnati is 3-2 on the season for the first time since making the Super Bowl during Chase's rookie year in 2021. The Bengals beat Miami 31-24 and didn't have any huge issues pop up after the game.

"Swayze (Bozeman) broke his forearm, so he'll go to IR," Taylor said about the latest updates. "Tanner Hudson has a pec issue that we're gathering more information on. Kyle Dugger (quad) still week to week. Those are really the main three right now in terms of guys that would be affected coming out of the bye."

The Bozeman blow stings, he has played 63 snaps for the Bengals on special teams this season.

The Bengals kept up with the rest of the AFC contenders this week and didn't lose any ground in the division. A group that could get really shaken up after Cincinnati's second division game of the season on Oct. 25 against Baltimore.

Cincinnati has two AFC wins so far and needs to amass as many as possible.

"Glad we won. Hard to win in this league. We've certainly been in those games before where we let them slip away and didn't get the win," Taylor said on Sunday. "Credit to Miami. They fought us tooth and nail till the very end. I thought Jeff Hafley is doing a great job with these guys, man. He's got them believing. They fought us like they fought a lot of other teams. They gave themselves a chance. There are a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown, gave them four points, and gave up over 200 yards rushing. Plenty to clean up.

"The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We've had some down-to-the-wire games the last three weeks. I know how hot this one was today. The bye week comes at a great time for us to be 3-2. These guys will regroup. We know who we are. Today, there are a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks."

The Bengals lick their injury wounds this week before preparing for Baltimore.

text:
Another day, another notable 49ers injury to monitor. This time, it's wideout Deebo Samuel, who injured his hamstring during the second half of San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks.

Samuels underwent further evaluation on Monday, and 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said that Samuel will be out "at least a couple of weeks." San Francisco will host Washington next week on "Monday Night Football." It will then face the Falcons in Atlanta in Week 7 before a Week 8 bye.

The injury occurred late in the third quarter with the 49ers trailing, 23-21. Samuel stayed on the ground for several moments after committing the 49ers' second turnover of the quarter. He fumbled the ball while running after a catch, and the turnover led to a Seattle field goal.

The 49ers responded with consecutive scoring drives. The first ended with a Brock Purdy touchdown pass to Brandin Cooks, who was recently signed to help the 49ers navigate through their injuries at receiver. The second drive was capped off by Eddy Pineiro's 44-yard field goal that proved to be the game-winning score.

San Francisco received a big game from Mike Evans, who caught seven passes for 113 yards and a score despite having two fractured ribs.

Evans and Cooks will have to continue to pick up the slack in Samuel's absence during the next several weeks. Samuel, 30, has had a successful reunion with the 49ers, who re-signed him this offseason after he spent the 2025 season with the Commanders. He's currently tied for second on the team with three touchdown catches and is second in receptions. He also has four runs that have resulted in first downs.

Despite their injuries, the 49ers are one of only three teams that are still undefeated. San Francisco currently has a two-game cushion over the rest of the field in the NFC West division.

text:
The Denver Broncos released their first estimated injury report of the week on Monday ahead of a Thursday Night Football showdown with the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 15.

Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and cornerback Pat Surtain (ankle) were listed as estimated non-participants Monday. The good news: cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) was an estimated limited participant.

Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine filled in as the team's two starting cornerbacks on Sunday and Devon Key stepped up at safety after Hufanga left in the third quarter.

Denver's secondary held up well against a depleted Los Angeles Chargers team in Week 5, but they'll face a much tougher test when Seattle and Jaxon Smith-Njigba visit Empower Field at Mile High on Thursday.

Elsewhere on the injury front, defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones (shoulder) was an estimated limited participant while safety Brandon Jones (foot) and guard Ben Powers (biceps) were estimated full participants.

The Broncos did not practice today, but the NFL requires teams to release three injury reports leading up to each game, so that's Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday for Denver this week. The team's only official practice of the week will be held on Tuesday.

The Broncos will release a final (estimated) injury report with game statuses on Wednesday.

text:
After the Green Bay Packers notched a much-needed division win over the Chicago Bears on Sunday, head coach Matt LaFleur seemed distracted in his postgame interview on local radio.

“It’s bittersweet for me right now because I just heard the news on Javon Hargrave,” he said. “It’s not good.”

Hargrave, the standout veteran defensive tackle, went down with less than 2 minutes to go and the Packers up 24. He will reportedly miss the rest of the season with a torn Achilles tendon.

During Fox’s broadcast, color analyst Greg Olsen illustrated the risks on both sides of navigating a blowout in the NFL. But he appeared to place most of the blame on Bears head coach Ben Johnson, who repeatedly called timeouts to extend the game and keep his team motivated despite the lopsided score.

“These are the kinds of games where [if] you’re the team winning, you’re just saying, ‘Get this thing over with,'” Olsen said. “You’re Ben Johnson, you’re extending the game, you’re always trying to speak to your team through your decisions of saying, ‘We’re gonna fight til the end.’ But at what cost?”

Olsen also addressed Packers faithful who might argue LaFleur should not have had Hargrave on the field.

“You never like to see anybody ever get hurt, but certainly in a 24-point game. And I think fans are going to think, ‘It’s a blowout, take everyone out,'” he explained. “Well, this isn’t college football. I don’t have 110 guys on the sideline in uniform.”

Olsen explained that most NFL teams have about one full set of defensive backups active on any particular game day. However, some are used on special teams or rotate with the starters. There are not enough substitutes to replace the entire lineup.

Of course, Olsen was not placing blame anywhere in particular for the freak injury. Hargrave was in a routine pass-rush situation when he seemingly tore the tendon. In football, any additional full-speed play brings significant risk of injury.
